items.title: DEP: Runtime-Free Router and Gateway On-Ramp

labels.name: router
labels.description: Relates to routing, KV-aware routing, etc.

items.body: ## Table of Contents - [Overview](#user-content-overview) - [Area](#user-content-area) - [Summary](#user-content-summary) - [Motivation](#user-content-motivation) - [Design](#user-content-design) - [Proposal](#user-content-proposal) - [Worker Identity, Tenant Isolation, and Schedulability](#user-content-worker-identity-tenant-isolation-and-schedulability) - [Selection Input and Admission Sequencing](#user-content-selection-input-and-admission-sequencing) - [Worker Topology and Platform Boundary](#user-content-worker-topology-and-platform-boundary) - [Engine Metadata Production](#user-content-engine-metadata-production) - [Interfaces](#user-content-interfaces) - [HTTP API](#user-content-http-api) - [In-Process Python API](#user-content-in-process-python-api) - [Existing Runtime-Backed Path](#user-content-existing-runtime-backed-path) - [Scope and Rollout](#user-content-scope-and-rollout) - [V1 Scope](#user-content-v1-scope) - [Phased Migration](#user-content-phased-migration) - [Requirements](#user-content-requirements) - [MUST](#user-content-must) - [SHOULD](#user-content-should) - [Open Questions](#user-content-open-questions) - [References](#user-content-references) ## Overview ### Area router, gateway ### Summary Migrate Dynamo routing toward a runtime-free router core and service API that can serve both Gateway/EPP selector-service integration and HTTP push-router/frontend use cases, while preserving the existing Dynamo-runtime-backed frontend/router path during migration. V1 is a practical runtime-free on-ramp; router-local parity and behaviors that require frontend, gateway, or worker coordination follow in later phases. ### Motivation The Dynamo router is one of the easiest Dynamo capabilities for users to want, but today the cleanest production paths often make router adoption feel like Dynamo runtime adoption. Existing vLLM/SGLang/TRT-LLM users frequently want a low-risk first proof: keep their current workers and request plane, add smarter KV/load-aware routing, measure TTFT/throughput, and roll back cleanly. The current Gateway API Inference Extension (GAIE) integration is pragmatic: the GAIE EPP framework is Go, while Dynamo's mature router lives in Rust under `dynamo-llm` and still assumes Dynamo runtime discovery, model config, preprocessing, worker state, and router bookkeeping. The result is Go EPP plugin glue plus CGO/C bindings into the existing Dynamo-native router. This preserves parity, but it is not the cleanest long-term on-ramp for runtime-free gateway or raw-engine deployments. ## Design ### Proposal Use the runtime-free selection service in `dynamo-kv-router` as the shared decision and accounting plane below Gateway and frontend integrations. Keep component ownership explicit: | Component | Owns | Does not own | | --- | --- | --- | | Selection service | Worker catalog, KV index, overlap/load scoring, scheduler queue, worker selection, and slot-tracker state | OpenAI protocol handling, raw-text tokenization, inference forwarding, or response streams | | Gateway adapter or frontend | Request normalization/tokenization, selection calls, dispatch, retries, lifecycle reporting, and response handling | A separate routing-policy implementation | | EPP topology adapter | Platform discovery, engine metadata probes, validation, and worker-catalog convergence | Selection or slot-tracker state | Support two integrations over the same selection service: 1. A thin Gateway/EPP adapter that requests a selection and writes routing hints while the Gateway owns the request/response path. 2. An HTTP push-router frontend that exposes OpenAI-compatible endpoints and owns forwarding, streaming, and slot-tracker cleanup. Query-only selection, select-and-reserve, and explicit select-then-reserve are caller workflows within this boundary, not separate service modes or routing implementations. Preserve the existing Dynamo-runtime-backed frontend/router path during migration. ### Worker Identity, Tenant Isolation, and Schedulability `worker_id` is globally unique across a selection-service deployment, not scoped by model or tenant. The topology adapter must use the same worker ID for that worker on every selector replica. A random `u64` is sufficient for the intended deployment scale: at one million generated IDs, the birthday-collision probability is approximately 1 in 37 million. `stable_routing_id` remains the optional identity used to preserve routing assignments across worker restarts. `tenant_id` provides logical tenant isolation and defaults to `"default"`. Each `(model_name, tenant_id)` pair owns a separate in-memory KV index, scheduler, and active-load partition, even when tenants submit identical hashes. This prevents one tenant's cache state, hash collisions, or poisoning from entering another tenant's routing decisions. Logical in-process separation does not guarantee resource-exhaustion isolation; deployments that need flood containment may require per-tenant quotas or service sharding. The registration schema is defined by [`WorkerRequest`](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/main/lib/kv-router/src/services/selection/types.rs). A schedulable worker requires a non-empty HTTP endpoint, a positive block size, and a positive DP size. DP start and size default to `0` and `1`. KV-event endpoints for every DP rank are required when KV events are enabled, and `max_num_batched_tokens` is required when queueing or a policy configuration is enabled. Replay, capacity, stable-routing, topology, Eagle, and KV-transfer fields are optional unless the selected policy requires them. Worker schedulability evaluation determines whether a catalog record contains enough compatible runtime data to select the worker safely. A valid record becomes `schedulable`; a record with missing or incompatible metadata remains `incomplete` and returns `not_schedulable_reasons`. Delete deactivates the worker and retains an `unschedulable` tombstone. This evaluation is local service behavior, not Kubernetes reconciliation. ### Selection Input and Admission Sequencing Selection normalizes two input forms into one policy path: - token input: the caller supplies `token_ids` or multimodal routing tokens, and the service computes block and sequence hashes - hash input: the caller supplies compatible `block_hashes`, `sequence_hashes`, and `isl_tokens` Raw-text normalization, chat-template rendering, and tokenization remain caller responsibilities. Selection requests may also include router overrides, expected output tokens, priority fields, pinned or allowed workers, routing constraints, and the `x-dynamo-meta-policy-class` header. Each selection-service replica owns its worker catalog, KV index, scheduler queue, and slot-tracker state. The EPP topology adapter applies the same worker catalog to every replica; selector replicas do not synchronize catalog changes. KV state can recover at startup through `/dump`. Admission, prefill-complete, and free events can be shared over best-effort ZMQ replica synchronization. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph A["Selector A"] AAPI --> AC["Worker catalog"] AC --> AIDX AC --> AS["Scheduler"] AS --> AST["Slot tracker"] end subgraph B["Selector B"] BAPI --> BC["Worker catalog"] BC --> BIDX BC --> BS["Scheduler"] BS --> BST["Slot tracker"] end T["EPP topology adapter"] -->|"worker CRUD"| AAPI T -->|"worker CRUD"| BAPI W["Workers"] -->|"KV events"| AIDX W -->|"KV events"| BIDX AST <-->|"best-effort lifecycle sync"| BST P["Recovery peer"] -.->|"startup /dump"| AIDX ``` A reservation is the slot tracker's handle for an active request. Adding a reservation records prompt-side and decode load on the selected worker. `prefill_complete` clears prompt-side load, and `free` removes the remaining active blocks. A reservation is accounting state used for load balancing, not an engine resource lease. `POST /select_and_reserve` makes selection and slot-tracker addition atomic only within the receiving process. Replica events may be delayed, reordered, or dropped, output-block updates remain local, and reservation IDs must be globally unique. `POST /select` followed by `POST /reservations` is likewise an explicit but non-atomic select-then-reserve flow. Strict cross-replica admission would require an authoritative sharded admission actor, versioned conditional booking, or an equivalent consistency protocol. ### Worker Topology and Platform Boundary The worker-catalog API above is the platform-neutral topology boundary. The selection service remains independent of Kubernetes APIs and resource types; Kubernetes reconcilers, static configuration, Dynamo-runtime discovery adapters, or other discovery systems all converge the same worker resource. Raw engines do not need Dynamo wrappers or Dynamo self-registration. The external topology reconciler owns the complete desired worker set and uses the worker CRUD API to converge every selector replica. Full relists recover from service restarts, watch interruptions, and missed events; incremental updates handle normal additions, changes, and removals. Replica synchronization carries slot-tracker lifecycle events, not catalog updates. ### Engine Metadata Production Kubernetes can discover a ready Pod and network endpoint, but it cannot infer resolved DP ranges, KV block geometry, effective capacity, or disaggregated-serving endpoints. The EPP's engine-specific topology adapter probes this post-startup metadata, normalizes and validates it as a selection-service worker record, and writes it through `/workers`. It creates, updates, or deletes registrations as worker runtime metadata changes. High-frequency load, queue, slot, and KV state do not flow through the worker-registration API. SGLang is the strongest initial target: - `/model_info` exposes model/tokenizer identity and capabilities. - `/server_info` exposes server arguments, scheduler-derived and per-DP state, engine version, and a structured KV-event publisher descriptor. - Together these appear sufficient for the aggregated-serving routing subset, subject to version-aware mapping and validation. vLLM is more fragmented: - `/v1/models` exposes served-model identity. - `/metrics` and `/load` expose live load and cache information, including `vllm:cache_config_info`. - `/server_info?config_format=json` exposes resolved scheduler, cache, and data-parallel configuration, but is development-only and not a stable production contract. The preferred vLLM direction is a stable upstream runtime-info endpoint. Until then, an adapter can combine stable HTTP/metrics surfaces with startup configuration or expose a thin engine-local normalized record. TRT-LLM still needs an equivalent minimum signal contract. Metadata probing and catalog updates must be retryable and idempotent. A ready Pod with incomplete runtime metadata remains inactive and is requeued; adapters must not guess DP, block-size, endpoint, or required capacity values. Registration itself is not expected to be the bottleneck at 1,000 to 10,000 workers, although convergence behavior depends on the external adapter. The more likely scale pressure is maintaining and processing many ZMQ KV-event streams. External testing has not identified a significant issue at 1,000 or more workers; Dynamo still needs internal validation at the 10,000-worker target. ## Interfaces ### HTTP API The first runtime-free foundation landed in #10641 and is available through `python -m dynamo.select_service`. It is built directly on `dynamo-kv-router`; it does not depend on `dynamo-runtime`, EPP/GAIE, or Dynamo worker registration, and it never forwards inference requests. This table is the canonical current HTTP surface for the DEP: | Resource | Operation | Current behavior | | --- | --- | --- | | Worker catalog | `POST /workers` | Upsert a worker record and return `201`. Reusing a globally unique `worker_id` replaces that record and reevaluates schedulability. | | Worker catalog | `GET /workers?model_name=...&tenant_id=...` | List the catalog, optionally filtered by model and tenant. There is currently no single-worker `GET`. | | Worker catalog | `PATCH /workers/{worker_id}` | Update supplied mutable fields and reevaluate scheduler/indexer activation. | | Worker catalog | `DELETE /workers/{worker_id}` | Deactivate and deregister the worker, then retain an `unschedulable` catalog record as a logical deletion/tombstone. | | Selection | `POST /select` | Return `worker_id`, `dp_rank`, endpoint, block size, tiered overlap, and effective prefill tokens without booking. | | Selection | `POST /select_and_reserve` | Select and add slot-tracker state in one operation local to the receiving replica; generate a reservation ID if omitted. | | Reservations | `POST /reservations` | Explicitly add a selected request to the slot tracker for select-then-reserve callers. | | Reservations | `POST /reservations/{id}/prefill_complete` | Clear active prefill load. | | Reservations | `POST /reservations/{id}/output_block` | Update local decode accounting; this high-frequency signal is not replica-synchronized. | | Reservations | `DELETE /reservations/{id}` | Free active-load state. | | Operations/read models | `GET /health`, `GET /ready`, `GET /loads`, `POST /potential_loads`, `POST /overlap_scores`, `GET /dump` | Expose liveness, schedulability, load/overlap inspection, and index recovery state. | The API uses structured JSON errors with HTTP semantics: malformed or inconsistent requests return `400`, missing resources return `404`, duplicate/failed bookings return `409`, overload can return `429`, and an unready service or rejected queue can return `503`. The service has no built-in authentication and is intended for a trusted internal network or an authenticated proxy boundary. The selection service does not support or intend to support a nested remote-indexer mode. A separately deployed indexer microservice is already remote when callers access it over the wire; the selection service does not forward worker registration to another indexer. `--indexer-peers` is limited to startup recovery through `/dump`. ### In-Process Python API The runtime-free core is also available in process through the feature-gated Python binding `dynamo.llm.SelectionService`. Its API mirrors the service operations for worker catalog management, readiness, selection and reservation lifecycle, and load/overlap inspection without an HTTP hop. ### Existing Runtime-Backed Path The existing `dynamo.llm.KvRouter` Python binding remains the Dynamo-runtime-backed push-router API during migration. The Dynamo-native frontend/router and current GAIE CGO bridge remain supported until parity, performance, and operational behavior are validated. ## Scope and Rollout ### V1 Scope The current implementation and API table define the V1 selection-service baseline. Remaining work is topology/metadata adapters and thin Gateway or frontend integrations, not another selection core. V1 preserves existing index recovery and worker replay behavior and reuses the shared scheduler's queueing, priority, routing-constraint, tiered-overlap, and output-block accounting primitives. The Gateway/EPP adapter translates GAIE requests and endpoints into selection calls and routing hints; routing policy remains in Rust. The optional HTTP push router owns forwarding and response lifecycle. Globally consistent cross-replica admission and new Gateway/frontend policy are follow-up concerns. ### Phased Migration 1. **Runtime-free aggregated selection core.** Establish the platform-neutral worker catalog, KV index, scheduler, selection API, and slot-tracker lifecycle. 2. **EPP/topology integration and scale validation.** Add engine-specific topology adapters, thin Gateway/frontend clients, and internal validation at 10,000 or more workers. 3. **Router-local parity.** Add the remaining local capabilities required by targeted integrations, including predicted routing, shared-cache lookup, queued-overlap refresh, overload handling, and additional prefill/load signals. 4. **Cross-component behavior.** Add behaviors that require frontend, gateway, or worker coordination, including rejection propagation, migration, retries, session affinity, and disaggregated prefill/decode orchestration. Full frontend/router parity remains the migration gate, but it is not the V1 gate. ## Requirements ### MUST - The selection core MUST be usable without `dynamo-runtime` or Dynamo worker registration. - Worker topology MUST use a platform-neutral, idempotent catalog API independent of Kubernetes resource types. - Worker IDs MUST be globally unique across a selection-service deployment and consistent across selector replicas. - Each `(model_name, tenant_id)` pair MUST use separate in-memory index, scheduler, and active-load state. - Raw-engine adapters MUST validate required endpoint, DP, block-size, and capacity fields and MUST NOT register guessed values. - The core MUST preserve token-aware tiered prefix scoring, worker eligibility, active-load accounting, slot-tracker lifecycle, and aggregated selection. - The API MUST provide query-only selection and local select-and-reserve without forwarding inference traffic. - Multi-replica selection MUST NOT be described as globally atomic without an authoritative consistency protocol. - The external topology adapter MUST converge the worker catalog on every selector replica. - V1 MUST preserve index recovery and worker replay behavior. - The existing Dynamo-runtime-backed router/frontend path MUST remain supported during migration. ### SHOULD - Gateway/EPP integration SHOULD remain a thin adapter to the selection API; Go should not contain a second routing implementation. - Kubernetes deployments SHOULD use an optional reconciler with engine-specific metadata probes; non-Kubernetes deployments should not require it. - The initial SGLang adapter SHOULD use `/model_info` and `/server_info`; vLLM SHOULD prefer a stable runtime-info contract and otherwise use stable surfaces plus startup configuration or a thin adapter. - Token and block-hash inputs SHOULD normalize into one selection policy; raw-text normalization and tokenization SHOULD remain outside the selection API. - The selection service SHOULD remain independently deployable from frontends and Gateway adapters. Further service decomposition should require measured scaling or failure-isolation evidence. - Push-router integrations SHOULD free slot-tracker state on success, upstream failure, and client disconnect. - Integrations SHOULD reuse existing scheduler policies rather than define a selector-specific policy model. - Scale validation SHOULD cover at least 10,000 workers, including catalog convergence, ZMQ listener fan-out, KV-event ingestion, recovery, and selection latency. - The design SHOULD benchmark in-process CGO against same-pod HTTP, gRPC, or UDS calls, including caller preprocessing and KV lookup costs. ## Open Questions - Which integration should consume the selection service first: Gateway/EPP, an HTTP push-router frontend, or both? - Is HTTP sufficient for the first integrations, or is gRPC/UDS required? - What reservation retry, failure, and stale-cleanup guarantees are required beyond the current API? - Which exact SGLang fields form the versioned normalized worker contract? - Should Dynamo propose a stable upstream vLLM runtime-info endpoint or own a thin normalization adapter? - What is the minimum TRT-LLM signal contract? - If best-effort replica synchronization is insufficient, which strict admission protocol should replace it? - What tenant sharding or quota boundary is required for resource-exhaustion isolation? - What acceptance criteria define the 10,000-worker scale target? - Which Phase 3 router-local parity capabilities should land first for the targeted integrations? ## References - Dynamo router guide: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/main/docs/components/router/router-guide.md - Dynamo GAIE guide: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/main/docs/kubernetes/inference-gateway.md - Current GAIE EPP adapter: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/tree/main/deploy/inference-gateway/epp - Current C bindings for GAIE/EPP router calls: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/main/lib/bindings/c/src/lib.rs - Standalone selection service guide and API: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/blob/main/docs/components/router/standalone-selection.md - Runtime-free selection service source: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/tree/main/lib/kv-router/src/services/selection - SGLang model/server introspection endpoints: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py - vLLM development-mode server-info endpoint: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/entrypoints/serve/dev/server_info/api_router.py

items.title: [P0] Isolate WordPress bridge data and authenticate plugin writes per site
items.body:
## Problem
WordPress bridge reads use raw persistence access that can bypass tenant isolation, while plugin writes use a fleet-wide secret and conflict with the global tenancy hook.

## Evidence
- `src/routes/wp-bridge.routes.js:239-265` exposes alerts, backups, reports, and hours.
- `src/services/wpBridge.service.js:325-389` performs reads through raw Prisma; omitted or caller-selected `siteUrl` can escape organization scope.
- WordPress bridge models in `prisma/schema.prisma:1580+` have incomplete organization ownership.
- `src/middleware/tenancy.js:30-76` does not implement the documented bridge exemption.
- Report, alert, hours, registration, and health writes rely on one fleet-wide body secret.

## Scope
Add organization ownership and staged backfill; use scoped Prisma for all reads; authorize site filters; authenticate every plugin write with per-site credentials or HMAC plus replay protection; reconcile middleware behavior; add two-tenant tests.

## Out of scope
Redesigning the fleet dashboard.

## Dependencies
#279; read-only production ownership audit; coordinated plugin rollout and secret rotation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every bridge table has enforceable ownership.
- [ ] Unfiltered reads return only the caller's organization.
- [ ] Cross-tenant reads and writes fail.
- [ ] Valid signed per-site writes succeed; wrong-site and replayed requests fail.
- [ ] Middleware and route authentication agree for all plugin endpoints.

## Verification steps
Use two organizations and two sites in integration tests; run production-like signed backup/report/alert/hour smoke tests; rehearse credential rotation.

## Risks
Incorrect backfill, plugin incompatibility, or rotation-related ingestion outage.

## Priority rationale
P0: confirmed tenant-data exposure risk and broken production ingestion path.

## External or human requirements
Production database audit, secret rotation, staged plugin deployment, and operations approval.

items.title: Decision: is Airbyte still on the roadmap? (ELT/ETL leaves scope under the multi-tenant direction)
items.body:
## Context

The local Airbyte setup uses `abctl`, which provisions Airbyte into a throwaway kind (k8s-in-docker) cluster on its own Docker network. This is a dev/POC convenience, not a production deployment. Several pain points encountered locally are artifacts of `abctl`, not the design:

- The Airbyte kind node must be manually bridged to the `open_epm` Docker network (`docker network connect open_epm airbyte-abctl-control-plane`), and **this bridge drops on every host reboot / Airbyte reinstall** — konsol then can't reach the Airbyte API (all calls fail until re-attached). Documented in `scripts/setup-airbyte.sh` but fragile.
- Airbyte API credentials are random per-install (`abctl local credentials`) and currently hand-pasted into konsol EPM Settings.
- `workspace_id` and `d365_source_definition_id` are found manually via the UI/API.

## What production should look like

Two viable shapes:

**A. Airbyte Cloud (managed SaaS)** — stable API (`api.airbyte.com`), OAuth application client-id/secret created once, stable workspace/source-definition IDs. The ClickHouse **destination** must be reachable from Airbyte Cloud (TLS public endpoint + IP allowlist, or tunnel/PrivateLink). D365 source side is already public HTTPS (Azure OData).

**B. Self-hosted Airbyte on Kubernetes (Helm)** — Airbyte + ClickHouse in the same cluster/VPC, **stable service DNS** (no docker bridge, no reboot-drop). Custom D365 connector image published to a registry (GHCR/ECR), versioned.

## What changes local → prod

| Concern | Local (abctl) | Production |
|---|---|---|
| Networking | manual `docker network connect`, drops on reboot | VPC/cluster service DNS (self-host) or secured endpoint/tunnel (Cloud) |
| Airbyte creds | random per-install, hand-pasted | secret manager (Vault / AWS Secrets Manager / K8s secrets), injected |
| workspace/source-def IDs | hunt in UI/API | set once via IaC (Terraform / Helm values / bootstrap) |
| EPM Settings Airbyte block | clicked in UI | provisioned by config/IaC at deploy time |
| D365 connector | local docker image | published, versioned registry image |
| Stability | reboot breaks it | restart policies, persistence, monitoring, HA |

## What stays the same

The konsol layer is prod-ready as-is: `provision_connector_airbyte` is idempotent (find-or-create), D365 creds stored encrypted in connector password fields, and the config → source → schema-apply → build flow is identical. Productionizing means swapping the Airbyte substrate, not rebuilding konsol.

## Multi-tenant (hosted-clients) notes

- One Airbyte workspace per client (or dedicated instance for isolation); connector → `workspace_id` scopes it.
- Per-tenant D365 creds stay encrypted in each tenant's konsol (never exposed to an LLM/MCP — only a `configured: true` boolean is ever returned).
- Per-tenant ClickHouse target (separate database/schema, e.g. `epm_raw_<tenant>`).
- Onboarding = IaC creating a workspace + connection + calling idempotent `provision_connector_airbyte`, not a human clicking buttons.

## Key decision

The single biggest real design decision is **how Airbyte reaches ClickHouse securely**: in-VPC service DNS (self-host) vs secured endpoint/tunnel (Cloud). Everything konsol-side carries over unchanged.

## Acceptance / next steps

- [ ] Decide Cloud vs self-hosted Helm
- [ ] Define ClickHouse-destination networking for the chosen path
- [ ] Move Airbyte + per-tenant secrets into a secret manager
- [ ] Provision EPM Settings Airbyte block + workspace/source-definition via IaC
- [ ] Publish the `source-d365-fno` custom connector image to a registry

---
_Filed from a working session analyzing the D365 → consolidation wiring on the local stack._

items.title: Engineering asset register (electrical/mechanical/plumbing/safety)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## Situation

The asset master (#286) gives FacilityConnect a generic maintainable-item record: identity, QR
payload, category, manufacturer, serial, location, criticality, lifecycle status and a
category-level JSON attribute schema. What it does not yet contain is the **engineering** content —
the actual class taxonomies and the class-specific attributes, relationships and derived state that
make an electrical asset behave like an electrical asset and a plumbing asset behave like a
plumbing asset.

A transformer is not meaningfully described by "manufacturer, model, serial". It has a rating in
kVA, a voltage ratio, a vector group, an oil volume, an oil-test regime, a tap-changer, and a
feeding relationship to downstream HT and LT panels. A distribution board has a parent panel, a
schedule of circuits, and a set of clinical areas it feeds. An air-handling unit has a filter bank,
a design air-change rate, and the rooms it serves. A dialysis water plant has a treatment train and
a sampling regime. Without those attributes and, critically, without the **feeds/serves**
relationships between assets, the platform cannot answer the questions that drive hospital
engineering: which clinical areas lose power if DB-4 is isolated; which AHU serves Theatre 2;
which pump set feeds the overhead tank that supplies the dialysis unit; which UPS backs the ICU
ventilator circuit.

The consequence of the absence is that every downstream capability degrades into a flat list.
Preventive maintenance (#291) can only schedule on category, not on rating or duty. Electrical
safety inspections (#629) have no panel hierarchy to walk. Generator and UPS availability (#311)
cannot state which areas lose standby power. Permit-to-work cannot compute isolation impact.
Breakdown reports (#293) cannot escalate on the basis that the failed asset feeds an ICU.

Affected roles: the **biomedical technician** and **electrician**, who scan an asset and expect its
rating, parent, downstream dependants and history; the **facilities manager** planning replacement
against expected life and condition; the **duty engineer** who must answer an isolation-impact
question in minutes; the **compliance owner** assembling evidence for an electrical inspectorate
visit under the Central Electricity Authority's 2023 electrical-safety regulations, or for a NABH
assessment; and the **ICU charge nurse**, who is the first person harmed when a dependency is
unknown.

One platform rule is non-negotiable here and is inherited from #286: medical gas, LPG/kitchen gas,
generator diesel, laboratory gases and refrigerant gases are **separate asset classes** and must
never share a generic "gas check completed" record. This issue must not create a shortcut that
undoes it.

---

## Task

### User or System Story

**As a** facilities manager and duty engineer
**I want** the engineering asset register populated with class-specific electrical, mechanical,
plumbing and safety attributes and with the feeds/serves relationships between assets and clinical
areas
**So that** maintenance regimes are correct for the asset type and the operational impact of any
asset failing or being isolated can be computed rather than remembered.

### Scope

**In scope**

* Class taxonomies under the #286 category tree, each with a validated attribute schema:
  * **Electrical** — transformers, HT panels, LT panels, distribution boards, circuit breakers,
    UPS systems, battery banks, diesel generators, automatic transfer switches, earthing systems,
    lightning protection, emergency lighting, isolation transformers, clinical-area power outlets,
    solar installations.
  * **Mechanical** — HVAC plant, air-handling units, chillers, cooling towers, boilers, pumps,
    motors, exhaust systems, ventilation systems, lifts and escalators, pneumatic tube systems.
  * **Plumbing** — water tanks, pump sets, pipework and valves, hot-water systems, sewage systems,
    drainage, water-treatment plants, reverse-osmosis plants, dialysis water systems, rainwater
    systems.
  * **Safety** — fire alarm panels, smoke detectors, sprinklers, hydrants, extinguishers, fire
    doors, emergency lighting, exit signage, gas detectors, panic alarms, CCTV, access control.
* Per-class attribute schemas with typed fields, units and validation (kVA, voltage ratio, litres
  per second, air changes per hour, ampere rating, IP rating, refrigerant type and charge), stored
  as validated JSON against a registered schema version so a new class does not require a
  migration.
* **Asset dependency graph**: typed directed relationships `feeds` (electrical/water/air supply),
  `backs_up` (UPS or generator backing a board), `serves_location` (asset to clinical area), and
  `part_of` (component to parent), with cycle prevention.
* Derived **impact query**: for any asset, the downstream assets and clinical areas affected by its
  failure or isolation, with a criticality roll-up.
* Class-driven defaults: default maintenance regime, default risk classification, default statutory
  obligation applicability and default required competency, all resolved through the rules engine
  from country, state, facility type, asset class, manufacturer recommendation and risk level —
  never hard-coded.
* Downtime history and condition per asset, feeding the asset-health measures in #646 and the
  maintenance dashboards (#294).
* Bulk import per class with dry-run validation and a per-row error report, because these registers
  are populated from existing spreadsheets at onboarding.

**Out of scope**

* The generic `asset` entity, QR generation, lifecycle status machine and document handling —
  #286; this issue extends it.
* Preventive-maintenance plan generation and checklist templates — #291 and #643; this issue
  supplies the class defaults they consume.
* Electrical statutory inspection execution and defect closure — #629.
* Generator load-bank and UPS battery test regimes — #630.
* Medical-gas plant, pipelines, valves and cylinders — #631, #632, #348; medical gas remains its
  own class with its own module and is deliberately not modelled as a generic mechanical asset.
* LPG, kitchen gas and fuel assets — #633.
* Lift statutory certification — #638 and #317.
* Meter and BMS telemetry ingestion — #645 and #296; this issue defines the meter attachment point
  only.

---

## Recommended Solution

Extend the FacilityConnect asset module (Go 1.26 / Gin / GORM, PostgreSQL 16 with RLS on
`tenant_id`) with a schema registry and a dependency graph. The design deliberately avoids one wide
table per class — a hospital has roughly 40 engineering classes and they change as the product
enters new facility types.

```sql
CREATE TABLE asset_class_schema (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id uuid,                  -- NULL tenant_id = platform-supplied schema
  class_code text NOT NULL,                              -- 'electrical.transformer'
  version int NOT NULL,
  json_schema jsonb NOT NULL,                            -- typed fields, units, ranges, required
  default_risk_class text NOT NULL,
  default_competency_code text,
  is_active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  UNIQUE (tenant_id, class_code, version));

CREATE TABLE asset_attributes (
  asset_id uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES asset(id),
  tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
  class_code text NOT NULL, schema_version int NOT NULL,
  attrs jsonb NOT NULL,
  validated_at timestamptz NOT NULL);

CREATE INDEX ON asset_attributes USING gin (attrs jsonb_path_ops);

CREATE TABLE asset_edge (
  tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
  from_asset_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES asset(id),
  to_asset_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES asset(id),
  edge_type text NOT NULL CHECK (edge_type IN ('feeds','backs_up','part_of')),
  medium text CHECK (medium IN ('electrical','water','chilled_water','air','steam','data')),
  notes text,
  verified_on date, verified_by uuid,
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, from_asset_id, to_asset_id, edge_type),
  CHECK (from_asset_id <> to_asset_id));

CREATE TABLE asset_serves_location (
  tenant_id uuid NOT NULL,
  asset_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES asset(id),
  location_id uuid NOT NULL,
  service_kind text NOT NULL,                            -- 'power','ventilation','water','fire_detection'
  is_critical_area boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, asset_id, location_id, service_kind));

CREATE TABLE asset_downtime (
  id uuid PRIMARY KEY, tenant_id uuid NOT NULL, asset_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES asset(id),
  started_at timestamptz NOT NULL, ended_at timestamptz,
  cause text NOT NULL CHECK (cause IN ('breakdown','planned_maintenance','statutory_isolation','awaiting_parts')),
  work_order_id uuid,
  CHECK (ended_at IS NULL OR ended_at > started_at));
```

Attribute validation runs in the service layer against the registered JSON Schema before write; an
attribute set that does not validate is rejected with per-field errors rather than stored. Schema
versions are additive — a new version may add optional fields, and existing assets are re-validated
lazily and flagged, never silently migrated, because a transformer whose kVA rating is absent must
be visible as incomplete rather than assumed.

`asset_edge` is a DAG per medium. Cycle detection runs on every edge write using a recursive CTE
and refuses the write naming the offending path; a cycle in an electrical distribution model means
the model is wrong, and returning a partial impact set from a wrong model is worse than returning
an error. Impact is computed by a recursive CTE over `asset_edge` unioned with
`asset_serves_location`, materialised into an `asset_impact` read model refreshed on topology
change, because the query is on the critical path of an isolation decision.

```
GET /api/v1/facility/assets/{id}/impact?edge_type=feeds
→ { "asset_tag": "DB-4-EAST",
    "downstream_assets": [{"tag":"SDB-3F-ICU","class":"electrical.distribution_board"}],
    "affected_locations": [{"name":"ICU 3F","is_critical_area":true,"service_kind":"power"}],
    "backed_up_by": [{"tag":"UPS-2","autonomy_minutes":22},{"tag":"DG-1","state":"available"}],
    "critical_area_count": 1,
    "topology_verified_on": "2026-05-14" }
```

`backed_up_by` is the operationally decisive field: isolating a board that feeds an ICU is
acceptable if a serviceable UPS and generator back it, and unacceptable if they do not. It is
resolved from `backs_up` edges joined to the standby-power readiness state published by #630, so
this issue consumes rather than duplicates that judgement.

API surface (`/api/v1/facility`):

* `GET /asset-classes`, `GET /asset-classes/{code}/schema`
* `GET/PUT /assets/{id}/attributes`
* `GET/PUT /assets/{id}/edges`, `DELETE /assets/{id}/edges/{to}/{type}`
* `PUT /assets/{id}/serves`
* `GET /assets/{id}/impact`, `GET /locations/{id}/supplying-assets` — the reverse query used when a
  ward reports a fault
* `GET/POST /assets/{id}/downtime`
* `POST /assets/import/dry-run`, `POST /assets/import/commit`

Events published: `facility.asset.attributes_updated.v1`, `facility.asset.topology_changed.v1`,
`facility.asset.downtime_started.v1`, `facility.asset.downtime_ended.v1`,
`facility.asset.critical_dependency_lost.v1`. The last is consumed by the work-order priority
engine (#648) and raises P0 when an asset serving an ICU, theatre or emergency department enters
downtime with no available backup. Consumed: `facility.workorder.started.v1` and
`.completed.v1` (downtime bracketing), `facility.standby_power.readiness_changed.v1` from #630.

OpenFGA:

```
type asset
  relations
    define facility: [facility]
    define viewer: staff from facility
    define can_edit_attributes: asset_engineer from facility
    define can_edit_topology: [user] or facility_manager from facility   # discipline-scoped
    define can_record_downtime: technician from facility or duty_engineer from facility
    define contractor_scoped: [user with time_window and work_order]
```

`can_edit_topology` is deliberately narrow and discipline-scoped: an electrical engineer may edit
`feeds` edges with `medium = 'electrical'`, not the chilled-water tree. The service checks both the
FGA relation and the discipline claim on the user's competency record. Contractors get
`contractor_scoped` tuples bound to a specific work order, asset and time window — read-only on
attributes, no topology editing, and no visibility of the wider estate.

Sequencing: #286 (asset master) and #288 (facility master) are hard dependencies; #627 provides the
locations that `asset_serves_location` points at. #291 and #643 consume the class default
maintenance regimes and should follow. #629, #630 and #638 all extend specific classes defined here
and depend on this issue landing first. #648's P0 escalation depends on
`facility.asset.critical_dependency_lost.v1`.

Risks: (1) an incomplete dependency graph returning a falsely small impact set — mitigated by
exposing `topology_verified_on` on every impact response, by requiring commissioning verification
before an asset can be used to gate an isolation, and by treating an unverified path as blocking
for non-emergency work; (2) attribute schemas proliferating per tenant until the register is
unqueryable — mitigated by platform-supplied schemas being the default and tenant overrides
requiring an additive-only diff check; (3) bulk import creating thousands of half-populated assets
— mitigated by dry-run validation, a mandatory completeness score per class, and blocking
`in_use` status until the required attributes for the class are present; (4) the gas-class
separation being eroded by someone modelling an oxygen manifold as a generic mechanical asset —
mitigated by validation that refuses to create a generic-class asset whose name or category
resolves to a gas class, and by medical gas living in its own module (#631).

---

## Acceptance Criteria

### Primary Scenario

**Given** the electrical class schemas are registered and transformer `TX-1`, panel `LT-1`, board
`DB-4-EAST` and sub-board `SDB-3F-ICU` exist
**When** the electrical engineer records `TX-1` attributes (1000 kVA, 11kV/433V, Dyn11), creates
`feeds` edges `TX-1 → LT-1 → DB-4-EAST → SDB-3F-ICU`, maps `SDB-3F-ICU` to serve ICU 3F as a
critical area, and adds a `backs_up` edge from `UPS-2`
**Then** the attributes validate against schema version 1 and persist; the topology is stored
acyclic; `GET /assets/{DB-4-EAST}/impact` returns `SDB-3F-ICU` downstream, ICU 3F as an affected
critical area and `UPS-2` under `backed_up_by` with its current autonomy; and
`facility.asset.topology_changed.v1` is published.

### Failure or Validation Scenario

**Given** an engineer attempts to create a `feeds` edge from `SDB-3F-ICU` back to `TX-1`, and a
mechanical technician attempts to edit the electrical `feeds` tree
**When** both writes are submitted
**Then** the first is refused with `409 topology_cycle` naming the path
`TX-1 → LT-1 → DB-4-EAST → SDB-3F-ICU → TX-1` and the prior topology is unchanged; the second is
refused with `403 discipline_scope` because the user's competency record carries no electrical
discipline, the attempt is audited, and no partial edge is written.

### Edge Cases

* An asset is created in class `electrical.transformer` with `kva_rating` omitted — the write is
  refused with a field-level error, and if created through bulk import the row is reported in the
  dry-run error report and the asset cannot leave `draft`.
* A schema version 2 adds an optional `oil_volume_litres` field — existing transformers remain
  valid, are flagged as incomplete against v2, and appear on a completeness report; nothing is
  auto-populated.
* A pump set is marked `part_of` a water-treatment plant that is itself `part_of` the pump set —
  refused by cycle detection; `part_of` is validated as a strict tree, not merely acyclic.
* `DB-4-EAST` enters breakdown downtime while `UPS-2` is itself under maintenance and no generator
  is available — `facility.asset.critical_dependency_lost.v1` is published, a P0 work order is
  raised, and the ICU charge nurse and duty engineer are notified within one minute.
* A contractor with a scoped tuple for work order `WO-118` on `AHU-4` requests
  `GET /assets/{TX-1}/impact` — refused with `403`, and their asset list returns only `AHU-4`.
* A ward refurbishment changes which AHU serves Theatre 2 but `asset_serves_location` is not
  updated — impact responses expose `topology_verified_on`, and any path unverified beyond the
  facility's configured re-verification interval blocks non-emergency isolation until re-verified.
* A user in tenant A requests `GET /assets/{id}/impact` for an asset ID belonging to tenant B — RLS
  yields no rows, the API returns `404`, and the recursive CTE is proven under test never to
  traverse an edge outside the session tenant.

---
## Engineering Guardrails

Complete the applicable items before the story is closed.

### Code Quality

* [ ] The change is limited to the agreed scope.
* [ ] Existing behaviour remains backward-compatible unless explicitly approved.
* [ ] Code follows the team's agreed standards and architecture.
* [ ] No temporary code, debug output or unnecessary complexity remains.
* [ ] Error handling is explicit and does not silently ignore failures.

### Test-Driven Development

* [ ] Acceptance criteria were converted into test scenarios.
* [ ] New or changed business logic was developed using Red–Green–Refactor where practical.
* [ ] Bug fixes include a regression test that fails before the fix and passes afterwards.
* [ ] Tests validate behaviour rather than private implementation details.

### Automated Testing

* [ ] Unit tests cover new and changed logic.
* [ ] Positive, negative and important boundary scenarios are covered.
* [ ] Integration or contract tests are updated where service boundaries change.
* [ ] Critical user journeys are covered by Playwright or an equivalent E2E framework.
* [ ] Existing tests pass.
* [ ] No new flaky or skipped tests are introduced without justification.

### Security and Access

* [ ] Authentication and authorisation are enforced at the appropriate layer.
* [ ] Users and services can access only the data and actions they require.
* [ ] Input is validated and sensitive information is not exposed in logs or errors.
* [ ] Secrets and credentials are not stored in source code.
* [ ] Security and dependency scans pass.
* [ ] Tenant, account or customer isolation is tested where applicable.

### Accessibility and User Journey

* [ ] The primary user journey works from start to completion.
* [ ] Loading, empty, success and error states are handled.
* [ ] Keyboard navigation and focus behaviour work correctly.
* [ ] Controls have clear labels and accessible names.
* [ ] The change meets the team's agreed WCAG accessibility level.
* [ ] The experience works across supported devices and browsers.

### Performance and Reliability

* [ ] The change does not introduce unnecessary API calls, database queries or processing.
* [ ] Timeouts, retries and failure behaviour are defined where applicable.
* [ ] Duplicate requests do not create inconsistent data.
* [ ] Performance-sensitive changes are tested against an agreed threshold.
* [ ] Partial failures do not leave the system in an invalid state.

### Observability

* [ ] Important failures are logged with useful diagnostic context.
* [ ] Logs do not contain sensitive information.
* [ ] Metrics or traces are added where the change affects a critical workflow.
* [ ] The team can determine whether the feature is working correctly after deployment.

### Documentation

* [ ] Relevant README, API or technical documentation is updated.
* [ ] Configuration or environment changes are documented.
* [ ] Deployment, migration or rollback steps are documented where required.
* [ ] Known limitations are recorded.

---

## Result

* Expected user or system outcome: any engineer can determine, in a single query, which clinical
  areas depend on a given engineering asset and whether serviceable backup exists, before isolating
  it — and every asset carries attributes rich enough to drive the correct maintenance regime.
* Expected business or operational outcome: preventive maintenance, statutory inspection
  applicability and work-order priority are all derived from asset class and criticality rather
  than assigned by hand, and no isolation of an asset feeding a critical area proceeds on an
  unverified dependency model.
* Success metric or validation method: ≥ 98% of engineering assets in the pilot facilities carry a
  complete, schema-valid attribute set for their class; 100% of assets serving ICU, theatre and
  emergency areas have a commissioning-verified `feeds`/`serves` path; `GET /assets/{id}/impact`
  p95 ≤ 300 ms on a facility with 4,000 assets and 6,000 edges; zero P0 escalations found
  retrospectively to have had an unmapped critical dependency over the monitoring period.
* Monitoring period, where applicable: 180 days from go-live, reviewed monthly at the engineering
  review and after each planned shutdown debrief.

---

---

## Pull Request Evidence

The pull request should include:

* [ ] Link to this story.
* [ ] Summary of the change.
* [ ] Test evidence.
* [ ] Screenshots or recordings for UI changes.
* [ ] Security, accessibility or performance evidence where relevant.
* [ ] Deployment and rollback notes for higher-risk changes.
* [ ] Known risks or follow-up work.

---

## Definition of Done

The story is complete when:

* [ ] All acceptance criteria pass.
* [ ] Required tests pass locally and in CI.
* [ ] No critical or high-severity security or quality issues remain.
* [ ] The critical user or system journey has been validated.
* [ ] Documentation is updated.
* [ ] Code review is complete.
* [ ] The change has been deployed or is ready for deployment through the standard pipeline.
* [ ] Post-deployment validation is defined or completed.
* [ ] Any exception is documented with an owner and reason.

---

## Exceptions

None — all guardrails apply. Topology editing is a console journey with a keyboard-operable
tree/graph editor and a table-based equivalent for screen-reader users; bulk import, dry-run
reporting and impact queries all have defined loading, empty and error states.

items.title: KB Ingestion Phase 4A: Multi-tenant ingestion observability daemon scaffold + telemetry schema
items.body:
## Context

Phase 4A sub-ticket of [#11628](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/11628) (Operations + Observability for Cloud-Native KB Deployments). Surfaced 2026-05-20 during nightshift-mode lane-pickup after parallel-track work on #11631 (Phase 0/1C-α write-side stamping by @neo-gpt) + #11660 (Phase 0/1B-β path externalization by @neo-opus-ada) + #11663 (Phase 4 retention policy by @neo-opus-ada).

**Pre-Phase-2-actionable per #11628 body escape clause:**
> *"Operator alerting + dashboard surfacing may begin in parallel once Phase 0/1 #11625 contracts land (daemon-scaffolding can start pre-Phase-2)."*

Phase 0/1A schemas + 0/1B registry are already on `dev`; Phase 0/1B-β paths (PR #11661) + 0/1C-α write-side stamping (PR #11662) are in @tobiu's merge gate. The daemon SHELL + TELEMETRY SCHEMA can land before Phase 2 #11626 ships its ingestion-service hooks — actual live-integration with Phase 2 ingestion calls is deferred to a follow-up sub-ticket.

## The Problem

After Phase 0/1 + Phase 0/1C-α land, cloud Agent OS deployments have:
- Stable `parsed-chunk-v1` + `backup-record-v1` schemas
- Source/Parser registry + per-source path config
- Write-side tenant stamping with `tenantId` / `repoSlug` / `visibility` / `originAgentIdentity`
- Configurable bundle retention

What's still missing for operational visibility:
- **No per-tenant ingestion metrics** — push frequency, error rates, ingestion latency, embedding-budget burn
- **No telemetry schema** for what metrics get persisted
- **No daemon orchestration** that wakes periodically to roll up + persist tenant-scoped metrics

The Phase 4 #11628 ticket's value-prop framing (operational-cost-of-recovery reduction, NOT data-loss prevention) anchors what 4A should collect.

## The Architectural Reality

Per [#11628](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/11628) Architectural Substrate Precedent — Phase 4A EXTENDS `KBRecorderService.mjs` rather than introducing a new substrate. KBRecorderService already persists every KB MCP tool invocation into the shared Memory Core SQLite database. Phase 4A adds:

1. **Per-tenant scoping**: extend the existing `kb_query_log` schema with tenant-aware columns (`tenantId`, `repoSlug`, `visibility`) OR add a sibling table `kb_ingestion_metrics` for ingestion-specific counts.
2. **Daemon orchestration**: new daemon at `ai/scripts/kb-observability-daemon.mjs` following the `orchestrator-daemon.mjs` / `swarm-heartbeat-daemon.mjs` pattern. Wakes on schedule; rolls up metrics; persists to MC SQLite.
3. **Telemetry-schema doc**: design doc at `learn/agentos/decisions/0NNN-kb-ingestion-telemetry-schema.md` (ADR) defining the persistence contract so Phase 4B reconciliation + Phase 4D alerting consume a stable schema.

## The Fix

### 1. Telemetry-schema ADR

Create `learn/agentos/decisions/0NNN-kb-ingestion-telemetry-schema.md`:

- What metrics are collected (per-tenant)
- Schema shape (column names, types, indexing)
- Retention policy (per-tenant — different from Phase 4 bundle retention)
- Consumer expectations (Phase 4B reconciliation, Phase 4D alerting, operator dashboards)

### 2. SQLite schema extension

Either:
- (a) Extend `kb_query_log` with `tenantId`, `repoSlug`, `visibility` columns (add migration)
- (b) Add sibling `kb_ingestion_metrics` table for ingestion-specific counts

Choice deferred to implementation — extension is simpler if metrics are query-call-shaped; sibling table is cleaner if metrics are roll-up-shaped.

### 3. Daemon shell

`ai/scripts/kb-observability-daemon.mjs`:

```js
import {KBRecorderService} from '../services/knowledge-base/KBRecorderService.mjs';
import mcConfig from '../mcp/server/memory-core/config.mjs';

// Wake on schedule (default: every 15 minutes).
// Roll up tenant-scoped metrics from kb_query_log (or sibling).
// Persist to a roll-up table for Phase 4D alerting consumption.

export async function runObservabilityDaemon({intervalMs = 15 * 60 * 1000, oneShot = false} = {}) {
    // ... implementation
}

if (import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`) {
    runObservabilityDaemon({oneShot: process.argv.includes('--once')}).catch(err => {
        console.error('[kb-observability-daemon] failed:', err);
        process.exit(1);
    });
}
```

### 4. Operator-facing CLI

`npm run ai:kb-observability` entry in `package.json` (one-shot mode for operator-driven manual rollup).

### 5. Tests

- Unit: `kb-observability-daemon.spec.mjs` — verifies rollup logic against synthetic `kb_query_log` rows with mixed tenants.
- Integration: synthetic multi-tenant fixture (reuse Phase 5 test fixtures once they land) — deferred to follow-up if Phase 5 fixtures aren't ready.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Telemetry-schema ADR drafted under `learn/agentos/decisions/` (number assigned at file time)
- [ ] SQLite schema extension OR sibling table added (impl decides between extending `kb_query_log` vs creating `kb_ingestion_metrics`)
- [ ] `ai/scripts/kb-observability-daemon.mjs` shell exists, follows existing daemon pattern, wakes on schedule
- [ ] Operator CLI `npm run ai:kb-observability -- --once` exists for manual rollup
- [ ] Unit test covers rollup against synthetic per-tenant rows
- [ ] Phase 2 live-integration hooks explicitly deferred to a follow-up sub-ticket (Phase 4A-β or similar)
- [ ] No regression to existing KBRecorderService behavior (manual smoke OR test assertion)

## Out of Scope

- **Phase 2 live-integration hooks** — Phase 2 #11626 doesn't exist yet; integration follows in Phase 4A-β post-Phase-2.
- **Phase 4D alerting surface** — separate sub-ticket. This phase collects + persists telemetry; alerting consumes it.
- **Phase 4B reconciliation daemon** — separate sub-ticket. Different concern (state-drift detection vs metrics rollup).
- **Phase 4C stale-chunk GC daemon** — separate sub-ticket. Different concern.
- **Per-tenant SLA / quota enforcement** — V1 surfaces the data; SLA enforcement is post-V1 commercialization scope per #11628 OOS.
- **Cross-deployment fleet management** — single-deployment scope for V1.

## Avoided Traps

| Trap | Why rejected |
|---|---|
| Building before Phase 2 ingestion-service exists | This sub-ticket scopes to scaffolding + schema only; live-integration deferred. The shell + schema ARE pre-Phase-2-actionable per #11628 escape clause. |
| New telemetry database | KBRecorderService already uses Memory Core SQLite; reuse the substrate. |
| Dashboard infrastructure | Out of scope for daemon work; sandman_handoff or portal app extension is Phase 4D territory. |
| Bundling rollup + alerting into one daemon | Separate concerns; testability + future modification budget benefit from separate daemons (per #11628 Avoided Traps). |
| Roll-up cadence baked into the daemon | Cadence becomes `aiConfig.kbObservability.intervalMs` config so operators can tune for high-volume vs low-volume deployments. |

## Related

- **Parent Phase Epic:** [#11628](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/11628) (Phase 4: Operations + Observability)
- **Parent meta-Epic:** [#11624](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/11624)
- **Substrate-extension target:** `ai/services/knowledge-base/KBRecorderService.mjs` (existing telemetry persistence)
- **Daemon precedents:** `ai/scripts/orchestrator-daemon.mjs`, `swarm-heartbeat-daemon.mjs`, `bridge-daemon.mjs`
- **Sibling parallel lanes** in flight:
  - PR [#11661](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/11661) Phase 0/1B-β path-externalization (@neo-opus-ada)
  - PR [#11662](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/11662) Phase 0/1C-α write-side stamping (@neo-gpt) — APPROVED, awaiting merge
  - PR [#11664](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/11664) Phase 4 retention policy (@neo-opus-ada) — APPROVED, awaiting merge
  - [#11646](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/11646) Phase 5C KB unit coverage expansion (@neo-gpt) in progress

## Origin Session ID

`7360e917-1733-4cdd-a6f3-5ac51c34b838`

- `ask_knowledge_base({query: 'KBRecorderService kb_query_log kb_query_faqs Memory Core SQLite telemetry', type: 'src'})`

Embeddings/pgvector hybrid retrieval deferred. Remaining: retrieval-quality eval harness (#43), allowlisted external fetch (#79).

items.body:
## Summary

Ground tutor responses in course materials: retrieve top-k chunks for the student's query, inject them into the prompt, and persist `citations` rows so answers are attributable. This is the "required for AI-PFTS + Clinical Informatics" capability from the data-model doc.

## Requirements

- [ ] `retrieveChunks(courseId, query, k)` — pgvector cosine top-k over `material_chunks`, org/course-scoped, with a similarity floor; embed the query with the same model as ingestion
- [ ] Injection point: retrieved context enters via the prompt builder (M4) as a clearly delimited context block with source labels — decide before-system vs tool-call retrieval and record the decision (start with always-retrieve-before-turn for determinism)
- [ ] Citations persisted: `citations` rows linking the assistant message → chunks actually provided (M2 schema)
- [ ] Chat UI renders source attributions on grounded replies (collapsible "Sources: …" with material name + page/slide) — design-system compliant
- [ ] Graceful behavior when a course has no materials: prompt unchanged, no empty context block
- [ ] Per-course toggle (materials exist but instructor can disable grounding)
- [ ] Vitest: retrieval scoping (cross-course isolation), citation persistence, no-materials path

## Context

- Retrieval quality tuning (hybrid search, reranking) is deferred to the eval-harness issue — this issue ships the straightforward cosine top-k loop



---

## Code Framework

### Files to create / modify

- `/Users/corderocore/Documents/llteacher/apps/web/src/lib/rag/retriever.ts` (new) — `retrieveChunks(db, courseId, query, k, similarityFloor)` using pgvector cosine distance top-k
- `/Users/corderocore/Documents/llteacher/apps/web/src/lib/rag/retriever.test.ts` (new) — unit tests with org/course scoping and similarity filtering
- `/Users/corderocore/Documents/llteacher/apps/web/src/db/schema/runtime.ts` (new) — define `citations` table linking polymorphically to `message` or `grade` via `citable_type + citable_id` (schema per `docs/architecture/multi-tenant-data-model.md` §6.3)
- `/Users/corderocore/Documents/llteacher/apps/web/src/server/routes/chat.ts` (modify) — after `messages: convertToModelMessages(...)`, inject retrieval: query embedding → top-k chunks → prepend to system prompt in a delimited `<retrieved_context>...</retrieved_context>` block
- `/Users/corderocore/Documents/llteacher/apps/web/src/server/routes/chat.ts` (modify) — on assistant message response, extract source chunk IDs from the context block (or store during retrieval) and create `citations` rows
- `/Users/corderocore/Documents/llteacher/apps/web/src/shared/types.ts` (modify) — extend `UIMessage` type to include optional `citations: { materialId: string; title: string; page?: number }[]`

### Pattern

Retriever: pure function (like `chunker.ts`) that takes db + params and returns `{ chunkId, material: { id, title, sourceType }, similarity }[]`.

Chat handler follows existing route structure; citations are captured server-side after the model response completes.

### Key types and skeleton

```typescript
// apps/web/src/lib/rag/retriever.ts
export async function retrieveChunks(
  db: Db,
  courseId: string,
  query: string,
  k: number = 5,
  similarityFloor: number = 0.3
): Promise<RetrievalResult[]> {
  // 1. Embed the query with the same model as ingestion
  const queryEmbedding = await embedText(query);
  // 2. pgvector cosine top-k scoped to courseId
  const chunks = await db.select(...)
    .from(materialChunks)
    .innerJoin(courseMaterials, eq(materialChunks.materialId, courseMaterials.id))
    .where(eq(courseMaterials.courseId, courseId))
    .orderBy(sql`${materialChunks.embedding} <-> ${queryEmbedding}`)
    .limit(k);
  // 3. Filter by similarity floor
  return chunks.map(c => ({ ...c, similarity: 1 - distance }));
}

// apps/web/src/db/schema/runtime.ts
export const citations = pgTable("citations", {
  id: uuid("id").primaryKey().defaultRandom(),
  citableType: pgEnum("citable_type", ["message", "grade"]).notNull(),
  citableId: uuid("citable_id").notNull(), // polymorphic
  materialChunkId: uuid("material_chunk_id")
    .notNull()
    .references(() => materialChunks.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
  spanStart: integer("span_start"),  // char offset if grounded to a span
  spanEnd: integer("span_end"),
  createdAt: timestamp("created_at", { withTimezone: true }).notNull().defaultNow(),
});

// In chat.ts after streamText response:
// Create citations rows for each chunk actually provided
if (retrievedChunks.length > 0) {
  await db.insert(citations).values(
    retrievedChunks.map(chunk => ({
      citableType: "message",
      citableId: messageId,  // the assistant message just created
      materialChunkId: chunk.id,
    }))
  );
}
```

### Pitfalls

- **Query embedding consistency**: The query embedding must use the same model + dimensions (1536) as chunking. Store the model version in code comments and cross-reference issue #40's embedding choice. A mismatch will silently fail (dimension error at runtime).
- **Org scoping in retrieval**: The FK join `courseMaterials.courseId` is the guard. Never skip the `eq(courseMaterials.courseId, courseId)` filter or a student could retrieve materials from a different course in the same org.
- **Similarity floor semantics**: Cosine distance is 1 - similarity (pgvector uses `<->` operator). A threshold of 0.3 similarity means distance ≤ 0.7. Document this in comments or a constant.
- **No-materials graceful path**: If `retrievedChunks` is empty (no materials or all below floor), do not prepend an empty context block to the prompt. The chat handler should detect this and proceed with an unmodified prompt (or log a metric).
- **Citations on both message and grade**: The polymorphic `citable_type` enum supports "message" and "grade". For now, only messages will cite. When grading is implemented (issue #51 or similar), ensure the same citations flow persists for feedback citations.
- **Prompt injection**: The retrieved context is untrusted instructor-uploaded text. Wrap it in XML delimiters (`<retrieved_context>...</retrieved_context>`) and add a system preamble warning the model not to execute instructions from the source material.

## Testing Strategy

**Must-cover risks:**

- **Cross-course retrieval isolation** — test that querying course A does not return chunks from course B, even if both are in the same org. Mocks a db with two courses and verifies the WHERE clause.
- **Similarity floor filtering** — test that chunks below the similarity threshold are excluded from results (even in top-k). Uses a fixture with known embedding distances.
- **Citation persistence on message** — test that creating a message + citations in the same transaction leaves both rows queryable. Catches FK issues or transaction rollback bugs.
- **Empty retrieval graceful path** — test that when retrieveChunks returns [], the prompt is not mangled (no empty context block, chat proceeds normally). Checks the injection logic in chat.ts.
- **No-materials course** — test that a course with zero materials returns [] with no errors. Verifies LEFT JOIN semantics and null handling.
- **Query embedding consistency** — test that the same query string, when embedded twice, produces the same or very similar vectors (for determinism in tests). Uses a mocked embedding endpoint.

**How:**

- Pure-function retriever tests: Vitest with a seeded in-memory db (or real Neon test DB per issue #83) and mock embedding results. Copy test patterns from `identity-cipher.test.ts`.
- Chat handler tests: extend `chat.test.ts` (create if missing) to mock retrieval results and verify citations are created. Mock the embedding provider.
- Integration test (optional): real materials in test DB + real chat flow, check citations appear in message response payload.

**Not worth testing:**

- pgvector distance metric math (PostgreSQL responsibility).
- Prompt-injection mitigation effectiveness (adversarial test in issue #43 eval harness, not unit scope).
- Citation UI rendering (component test in issue #42, admin console)

## OWNER PRIORITY OVERRIDE — USABLE GENERAL-PURPOSE STRUCTURAL PARSER BETA (2026-10-18)

**Latest owner decision / highest execution priority. This supersedes earlier ACC-E1–E5 *physical manufacturer wire / firmware / matched relay PCAP / vendor-native typed Oracle* prerequisites as P0 work and as release-readiness gates. Preserve past ACC/STD evidence and worktrees, but stop indefinite evidence chasing.**

### What Parser Studio is for
Deliver a **usable, vendor-agnostic Auto Parser**, not a universal 100%-correct manufacturer semantic decoder. **Structural parsing success and ordinary user task completion are the primary KPIs.** Prefer generic framing, stream record boundary recognition, structural candidate selection, reuse of JSON / Syslog / KV / CSV / CEF / LEEF / W3C / Zeek grammar, supported mixed-event handling, exposed residuals, and bounded deterministic multi-pass over vendor-specific regex patches. A broad security log should be useful even where semantics or a few fields require human correction.

### Success metrics / evidence policy
1. **P0 structural event coverage** = number of original event records safely detected and structurally extracted / total original events in representative security corpora. Report **PARSED, PARTIAL/REVIEW, RAW_ONLY/UNSUPPORTED** separately. Track per-family (not only aggregate) counts, source records/accounting and before/after against the same baseline. The earlier tuned datasets (535/571 = 93.7% across Juniper/Check Point/Sophos/CrowdStrike; 777/790 = 98.4% across PAN/Umbrella/Defender) are *existing development reference points*, not independent global manufacturer-accuracy or new unseen performance claims. Do not force unsupported formats into PARSED solely to raise the count.
2. **P0 safe usability**: a new user can paste/upload samples, run Auto Parser, see parsed fields and exact unparsed/residual regions, review/change CSV column order or declared prefix where applicable, revise mappings, and perform a supported DRAFT parser creation/test/download using the existing two creation methods. When Auto Parser cannot finish, ChatGPT Assisted Parser must offer explicit user-redacted/manual correction with validation and review. Do not revive Wizard/Workbench or require regular-expression expertise.
3. **P0 bounded safety**: zero silent record loss, no invented complete events, no crashes/hangs in the bounded representative acceptance set, no falsely claimed native/device/target verification, no automatic raw customer data transfer, and no dangerous/generated parser code execution. Unknown input may stay PARTIAL/RAW_ONLY with actionable recovery. Field semantics or typed values without independent truth must be marked unverified, not falsely certified.
4. **P1 optional precision**: full original UTF-8 byte spans, manufacturer-specific empty/duplicate/escape interpretations, firmware-specific native meaning, authenticated producer/relay packets and physical-device field F1 are **NON-GATING research/backlog**, only revisit for a customer-visible blocker, common grammar defect, or explicit owner request. Historical 197 REVIEW_ONLY remain non-promotable absent sufficient source evidence; this is not a mandate to solve them before beta.
5. **Target/runtime honesty remains mandatory**: beta can present a validated DRAFT and known supported adapters, but never claim proprietary Stellar DP/sensor/Native integration unless actually validated. Existing governance, authorization for real production/DP/sensor/credentials, merge/release, and security/privacy policies remain in force.

### Short, finite P0 implementation and acceptance roadmap (in order)
- **USE-0 / baseline inventory:** verify actual current product/dev backend, exact Git/PR/dirty state, two-path integrated product behavior and existing features; do **not** rerun completed #83–#87/P0-STD qualification. Prefer known clean code and preserve frontend 11/backend 10 intentional dirty files.
- **USE-1 / bring working structural engine to the actual user flow:** evaluate current Auto Parser vs completed generic Multi-Pass/Generic Structural/Funnel capabilities; selectively integrate *only product-relevant, qualified* general fixes in a new isolated development integration lane (no mutation of protected product worktree/main). Prioritize mixed security logs, envelope/prefix, CSV schema, field output and partial recovery. Do not integrate all research-only observers or create another research PR without a direct user benefit.
- **USE-2 / short structural coverage gate:** run a **finite representative multi-vendor, multi-format structural batch**, using existing pinned 571/790 references where applicable plus a concise cross-family smoke including invalid records; record per-format PARSED/PARTIAL/RAW, event accounting, before/after and zero false-complete/data loss. An earlier scored corpus is regression evidence, not a newly blind score. Fix confirmed general parser defects, not manufacturer-tailored patches.
- **USE-3 / first-time user E2E:** perform the complete real Web UI Auto Parser and ChatGPT Assisted user flow on the same candidate/dev backend, including CSV field schema, corrections, result review and DRAFT generation. Fix only actual P0 blockers and serious beginner usability defects; stop repeating unchanged tests. Full, same-HEAD checks for changed code, including browser/localhost integration, remain necessary.
- **USE-4 / usable beta candidate:** make the finite acceptance checklist and known limitations visible; once P0 flows work, expose a development-only beta for owner hands-on use (no public/prod/DP/sensor deploy or PR merge without separate approval). Subsequent improvements are prioritized from real usage, failure categories, and owner feedback.

**Execution policy:** Do not wait for genuine manufacturer on-wire captures, firmware/relay attestation or perfect field semantic F1 before moving to a useful product. Do not pretend results are more accurate than demonstrated. The newest Issue #1 ACTIVE/NEXT_CHAT_START must point to this generalist usable-beta execution priority, not older ACC producer-original tasks.

Reuse visual tokens: orange #f05b29, gold #f8ae41, charcoal #231f20, navy #11131a, canvas #f5f5f6, white panels, line #dfdddf, green #138a63, red #c83f4d, blue selection #3549a5, Inter/system font, white header with orange top border, 8–14px radii, subtle shadows, responsive layout. <!-- OWNER_FINAL_AUTO_POC_AND_DUAL_AI_RECOVERY_20261014 -->
## OWNER P0 DECISION — Final Auto Parser PoC, then dual AI recovery (2026-10-14)

**Current execution priority:** P0-E1 final bounded accuracy-first Multi-Pass improvement → P0-E2 evidence-based engine PoC decision → P0-AI1 whole-log fallback → P0-AI2 selected-region repair → P0-AI3 verified Recipe/native output → P0-AI4 two-path UI E2E. This supersedes older roadmap priorities only for the active engine/fallback sequence. Do not interrupt runnable engine work for unrelated UI.

**Mandatory two cases inside the existing two authoring methods:**
- **Entire-log AI assistance** when automatic parsing is RAW_ONLY/unsupported. User reviews/redacts and copies the full-log prompt, manually imports a schema-valid v0.2 Recipe; no automatic raw-log egress.
- **Selected-range AI correction** for PARTIAL/unparsed or already-parsed-but-wrong/unwanted fields. Highlight exact source spans, allow mouse/touch selection and field click, explain current rule/claims and user desired fields, generate scoped prompt, import a validated rule, show before/after and guard all unaffected accepted fields. User explicitly approves replacements. No third creation method or legacy Wizard/Workbench.

**Engine PoC exit:** Keep pre-registered `ENGINE_POC_ACCEPTANCE.md` gates (>=500 genuinely new unique events / >=5 products / >=3 formats / >=2 new version/subtypes; exact native path/value/type/UTF-8 span F1 >=99%, exact event rate >=95%, zero false-complete/raw loss/exceptions, two fresh defect-free batches, full regression + exact-head CI). If all PASS, close PoC. Otherwise publish **ENGINE_POC_LIMITED / NOT QUALIFIED** and freeze best verified engine candidate, route remaining unsupported source regions to AI assistance; never call a failed gate PASS.

**Current actual engine HEAD at roadmap write:** `e0bee5536f84a7a0cf9868954891cedc09372c15` on `poc/security-stream-framing-20261014`, Draft PR #16. Last engine source change `ccccbfc` passed 298/298 local regression. items.title: [DOCS] Canonical docs relay queue — Khế MVP
items.body:
## Purpose

Đây là **single pinned queue** cho mọi report cần fold vào canonical docs (BRD / SRS / Glossary / PROJECT_PLAN / CLAUDE.md / Mockup).

**Owner:** ERP_Docs session (branch `claude/edit-git-docs-Khe01`). Single-owner. Reads queue → folds canonical → replies `✅ Folded — <version>`.

**Posters:** All session leads after PR merge (post-merge rule).

---

## Post-merge rule (BẮT BUỘC)

Trong vòng **24h** sau khi PR merge vào `main` (hoặc `staging` nếu spec-impact cần frontend sync sớm), session author MUST comment vào issue này với template dưới đây.

Bỏ qua = rule violation, ERP_Docs sẽ flag trong Weekly Review.

Áp dụng khi PR ảnh hưởng tới: **business rule, schema, API contract, UI, deploy info, hoặc known bug**.

---

## Comment template

```
### <YYYY-MM-DD> — <session_name / branch>
- **PR / trigger:** #<số PR> → `<base branch: main hoặc staging>`
- **Đã đụng:** <file / module / area, vd backend/modules/ingest, frontend/src/pages/admin/Documents.jsx>
- **Thay đổi:** <1-3 dòng tóm tắt cái gì thay đổi và tại sao>
- **Docs cần cập nhật:**
  - BRD §<x> (vd §4 nguyên tắc / §7 functional)
  - SRS §<y>
  - Glossary (terms cần thêm/sửa)
  - PROJECT_PLAN (milestone update)
  - CLAUDE.md (bug pattern / business rule / API field mapping)
  - "chưa rõ" nếu uncertain
- **Ambiguity / cần PM xác nhận:** <nếu có spec conflict hoặc cần ratify, hoặc "none">
```

---

## ERP_Docs workflow

### Session kickoff

1. Read this issue's comments (sort newest first).
2. Categorize comments by status:
   - **Pending** — chưa fold
   - **Processed** — đã fold (reply marked ✅)
3. Process pending in chronological order.

### Cascade fold order

**BRD → SRS → Glossary → PROJECT_PLAN → CLAUDE.md → Mockup**

Reasoning: business rule (BRD) drives spec (SRS) drives terminology (Glossary) drives planning (PROJECT_PLAN) drives operational notes (CLAUDE.md). Mockup last (UI follows spec).

### Per-fold actions

For each canonical doc updated:
- Bump version number trong header
- Add changelog entry (đầu file hoặc separate changelog section)
- Cross-check references to other docs (no broken §x links)
- Reply DOCS_INBOX comment với: `✅ Folded — BRD v0.2 + SRS v0.3 + CLAUDE.md v0.5`

### Pre-commit check (BẮT BUỘC)

Trước khi `git commit` cho thay đổi BRD/SRS/GLOSSARY/PROJECT_PLAN:
- Verify cascade consistency (no stale cross-references)
- Verify version bumps
- Verify DOCS_INBOX comments reply marked

### Weekly Review (Monday)

Đầu mỗi session docs-editor Monday, run 8-item checklist:

- [ ] DOCS_INBOX có pending comments > 7 ngày? Process immediately.
- [ ] BRD version cao hơn SRS version → sanity check cross-ref
- [ ] Glossary terms còn match BRD/SRS use cases?
- [ ] PROJECT_PLAN milestone status đồng bộ với GitHub issue status?
- [ ] CLAUDE.md "Common Bug Patterns" có entries mới từ INC trong tuần?
- [ ] Mockup files version match current spec?
- [ ] No "TBD" / "TODO" entries trong canonical docs > 2 sprints? File issue.
- [ ] PM_Assistant STATE file recent updates? Cross-check decisions ratified vs draft.

Append findings vào `## Weekly Review Log` section dưới đây.

---

## Section: Pending

*(ERP_Docs ngầm: keep this section ordered newest-first; move processed entries to ## Processed below.)*

<!-- Posters: post new comments BELOW this section header (chronological). -->

---

## Section: Processed

*(ERP_Docs: move entries here sau khi fold xong + reply ✅.)*

---

## Section: Weekly Review Log

*(ERP_Docs: append weekly Monday review findings here.)*

```
### <YYYY-MM-DD> Weekly Review

- 8-item checklist results: <pass/fail summary>
- Pending count: <N>
- Issues filed: <list>
- Next review: <YYYY-MM-DD>
```

---

## Notes

- Owner is single ERP_Docs session — không spawn parallel docs-editor sessions (sẽ conflict).
- ERP_PM_Assistant có thể post initial comments cho bootstrap (e.g., relay BRD v0.1 → fold sau ratify).
- Sessions không có write permission lên `docs/` — bắt buộc qua queue này.
- Issue này luôn `status:in-progress` (long-lived). Comments là work units, not issue lifecycle.
