items.title: E2: Per-tenant event ingestion quota (100k/day, durable Postgres counter)

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

items.body:
## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** Enforce a per-tenant daily event ingestion cap using a durable Postgres counter, replacing the in-memory rate limiter for the hosted deployment path only.

**Depends on:** #44 (E1 — needs `tenant_id`/`withTenant` plumbing in place).

**Current behavior:**
The existing rate limiter (`isRateLimited()`) uses an in-memory `Map`. This works for self-hosted (single, long-running process) but is not a real limit in a serverless deployment — a cold-start invocation has fresh memory, so the counter does not actually accumulate state across invocations. There is no per-tenant event volume cap anywhere in the codebase, and no cost-recovery mechanism exists (v1.0 has no billing), so nothing currently stops one tenant from consuming unbounded shared infrastructure.

**Desired behavior:**
A `tenant_quotas` table (`tenant_id`, `events_today INTEGER DEFAULT 0`, `quota_date DATE DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE`, `events_daily_cap INTEGER DEFAULT 100000`) tracks each tenant's daily event count. Inside the event-ingestion path, in the same transaction as the event insert (via `withTenant`):
1. If `quota_date < CURRENT_DATE`: reset `events_today = 0`, `quota_date = CURRENT_DATE`, atomically.
2. If `events_today >= events_daily_cap`: reject with HTTP 429 and a `Retry-After` header (seconds remaining until UTC midnight) — before the event is written.
3. Otherwise: insert the event and increment `events_today` atomically, in the same transaction.

The self-hosted deployment path keeps the existing in-memory limiter unchanged (it works correctly there — single process, memory persists between requests). The hosted deployment path uses this Postgres-counter implementation instead, behind the same `isRateLimited()`-shaped interface, selected by environment — this should read as a drop-in alternate implementation, not a rewrite of the self-hosted behavior.

The cap (`events_daily_cap`) is visible to the founder in Settings/Dashboard as "X / 100,000 events today" — never a silent wall.

A separate, lower-frequency mechanism (not part of the hot ingestion path) sums `events_today` across all tenants and compares it to a known fraction of the hosted Postgres provider's plan-level compute capacity, logging/emailing an alert if crossed. This is a monitoring signal for a human decision (pause signups, upgrade plan), not an automatic per-request action.

**Key interfaces:**
- `tenant_quotas` table schema as above
- The event-ingestion function's tenant + quota-aware extension (the existing `processEvent()`-shaped seam)
- `events_daily_cap` must be adjustable per-tenant without a code deploy (it's a plain column, not a compiled constant)
- The aggregate monitor — a scheduled job, reusing whatever scheduling mechanism the deployment already has for keep-alive pings (see #42/H1)

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] An event under quota is accepted and `events_today` increments by exactly one
- [ ] An event at exactly `events_daily_cap` is accepted; the next one for that tenant is rejected
- [ ] A rejected event returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header equal to seconds remaining until UTC midnight
- [ ] The quota resets correctly across a UTC-day boundary
- [ ] Two tenants with different `events_daily_cap` values are limited independently and correctly
- [ ] Self-hosted deployment continues to use the existing in-memory limiter, unmodified in behavior
- [ ] The founder-visible quota indicator reflects the real counter value
- [ ] The aggregate monitor alert fires when total ingestion crosses the configured threshold (test with a mocked/lowered threshold)

**Out of scope:**
- Any billing or paid-tier logic
- Redis, Upstash, or any external rate-limiting service — this stays entirely in Postgres
- Session replay's separate storage quota (see E4)

items.title: Phase 4A — Per-Tenant Ingestion Observability Daemon (KBRecorderService Extension)
items.body:
## Context

Sub of Phase 4 Epic [#11628](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/11628) (meta-Epic [#11624](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/11624)).

**Extends existing KBRecorderService for multi-tenant telemetry.** No new database; reuses Memory Core SQLite substrate per `KBRecorderService` precedent.

## The Problem

Once Phase 2 push pipeline ships, cloud operators have no visibility into per-tenant ingestion health: push frequency, error rates, ingestion latency, embedding-budget burn, schema-version drift, etc. Without observability, operators can't:

- Detect tenant abuse (excessive pushes, embedding budget exhaustion)
- Detect tenant errors (silent push failures, schema mismatches)
- Plan capacity (per-tenant chunk growth rates)
- Surface health in operator dashboards

## The Fix

Extend [`KBRecorderService.mjs`](../tree/dev/ai/services/knowledge-base/KBRecorderService.mjs) (currently captures KB QUERY telemetry → projects to `kb_query_faqs`) to also capture INGESTION telemetry:

1. **New SQLite table `kb_ingestion_events`** in shared Memory Core database:
   - `tenantId`, `agentIdentity`, `eventType` (push/parse/embed/error), `timestamp`, `chunkCount`, `durationMs`, `bytesIngested`, `errorCode?`, `schemaVersion`
2. **`KnowledgeBaseIngestionService.ingestSourceFiles` (Phase 2A) emits telemetry events** to `KBRecorderService.recordIngestionEvent({...})`
3. **Aggregation projection** (similar to `kb_query_faqs`): per-tenant rolling-window metrics materialized into `kb_tenant_ingestion_health` table
   - Per-tenant push frequency (events/hour)
   - Per-tenant error rate (errors/total)
   - Per-tenant chunk growth rate
   - Per-tenant embedding-budget burn (chunks × embedding cost)
4. **Daemon process**: `ai/scripts/kb-observability-daemon.mjs` (sibling to existing daemons) runs aggregation projection periodically + writes to `sandman_handoff.md` health section

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `kb_ingestion_events` table schema defined + migration
- [ ] `KBRecorderService.recordIngestionEvent` method implemented
- [ ] Phase 2A `KnowledgeBaseIngestionService` emits events at all lifecycle hooks (push received, parse complete, embed complete, error)
- [ ] `kb_tenant_ingestion_health` aggregation projection materialized
- [ ] Daemon `ai/scripts/kb-observability-daemon.mjs` exists; follows existing daemon pattern (orchestrator-daemon precedent)
- [ ] Daemon emits health summary into `sandman_handoff.md` under `## KB Multi-Tenant Health` section
- [ ] Unit tests: event recording, aggregation projection, daemon scheduling
- [ ] Integration test: multi-tenant push simulation → daemon aggregation → sandman_handoff.md health section populated

## Out of Scope

- Operator alerting on thresholds → Phase 4D
- Reconciliation logic → Phase 4B
- Stale-chunk GC → Phase 4C
- External dashboards / Grafana / Prometheus (sandman_handoff + portal app is V1 substrate; external dashboards is later)

## Related

- **Parent:** [#11628](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/11628)
- **Blocked-by:** Phase 2A (#TBD — `KnowledgeBaseIngestionService` must emit events)
- **Daemon pattern precedent:** `ai/scripts/orchestrator-daemon.mjs`, `swarm-heartbeat-daemon.mjs`, `bridge-daemon.mjs`
- **Substrate extension:** `KBRecorderService.mjs` (existing telemetry collector)
- **Sandman integration:** `GoldenPathSynthesizer.renderConsumerFrictionSection` pattern (PR #11622 sibling)

## Origin Session ID

`7360e917-1733-4cdd-a6f3-5ac51c34b838`

## Handoff Retrieval Hints

- `KBRecorderService.mjs` is the extension target — read it first
- `GapInferenceEngine` (referenced in KBRecorderService) is the projection-consumer architectural pattern
- `ai/scripts/orchestrator-daemon.mjs` is the daemon-scheduling pattern reference

items.title: Integrations: Gmail and Google Contacts sync - two-way email and contact data flow
items.body:
## 1. Executive Summary

Let a rep connect their personal Gmail inbox and Google Contacts (via the OAuth/credential infrastructure built by the sibling issue **"Integrations: Third-party connection hub - admin-managed credentials for Google Workspace and Calendly"**) so that (a) Gmail messages to/from a lead's known contacts are pulled into this app's existing unified activity timeline, and (b) a rep can pull a person from their Google Contacts onto a specific lead as a new contact. This issue is scoped to the **data-sync logic only** — periodic Gmail polling, matching, dedup, and a one-way Contacts import — built entirely on top of the hub issue's credential store. It does not build OAuth, token storage, or any connection-management UI itself.

## 2. Business/Product Context

The repo owner's standing direction for all future roadmap work is to "always consider 3rd party integration opportunities such as google contact, google calendar, gmail, calendly, etc — where the user can add their API/Secret whatever required to connect." Reps already correspond with leads from their own personal Gmail outside this app's dedicated Resend inbound address, and already have lead contacts saved in their personal Google Contacts before those contacts ever reach this CRM. Both are currently invisible to the app. Surfacing that existing activity/contact data — without asking a rep to change how they already work in Gmail — closes a real visibility gap in the per-lead activity history and contact directory this app already invests in (issues #138–#142).

## 3. Current State (verified by direct code read)

- **Unified activity timeline** (issue #140): `app/lib/activity-log-store.ts` defines `ACTIVITY_LOG_COLLECTION = 'activityLog'`, `ActivityEntryType = 'email-outbound' | 'email-inbound' | 'note' | 'system'`, and `ActivitySource = 'inbound-webhook' | 'manual' | 'outreach-log'` (lines 15–16). `ActivityLogDocument` (lines 48–71) carries an `externalId?: string` field described explicitly as "the originating provider's own message identifier (Resend's email_id)... Only ever set by inbound-webhook writes," backing a **unique, sparse** index (`ensureActivityLogIndexes`, lines 82–92) that makes a provider's webhook retry a no-op instead of a duplicate. `GET /api/leads/[id]/activity/route.ts` (lines 18–24, 48–67) merges `activityLog` docs with `outreach_logs` docs at read time via `mergeActivityTimeline()` — there is only ever one merged timeline, never a second parallel one.
- **UI**: `app/components/ActivityPanel.tsx` fetches that same merged endpoint and renders it (lines 51–77, 111–162). Its **local** `ActivityEntry` type (lines 6–14) independently re-declares `source: 'inbound-webhook' | 'manual' | 'outreach-log'` — this union must be extended in lockstep with `app/lib/activity-log-store.ts`'s own `ActivitySource`, or a new source value narrows correctly server-side but fails to type-check / render meaningfully client-side.
- **Contact-reply matching** (issue #142): `lib/contact-reply-matching.ts`'s `matchReplyToLeads(db, brand, tenantId, senderEmail)` (lines 54–80) looks up leads by `contactEmails: email` (an indexed, denormalized array — `contacts.ts`), returning `{kind: 'no-match'} | {kind: 'single-match', leadId} | {kind: 'multi-match', leadIds}`. `findMatchedContact()` (lines 86–107) re-resolves the specific `NormalizedContact` within a matched lead. `generateContactSuggestion()` (lines 140–184) parses a reply's signature block and writes a **pending, human-reviewable** suggestion to a `contactSuggestions` collection — it never writes `contacts[]` directly, matching the repo's established never-auto-merge stance (issue #137, `/admin/duplicates`).
- **Contact model**: `lib/contacts.ts`'s `NormalizedContact` type (lines 17–45), `normalizeContact()` (118–151), `dedupeContacts()` (183–224), and `contactKey()` (158–164: `name+phone` > `name+email` > bare `name`, lowercased) are the single shared normalization/dedup path used identically by every lead write route (POST/PUT/PATCH-MODIFY), replacing three previously-diverging implementations (issue #45). `deriveContactEmails()` (232–238) and `ensureContactEmailsIndex()` (246–254) keep the `contactEmails[]` index in sync on every write.
- **Existing inbound-email path** (issue #141): `lib/resend-webhook.ts` verifies Resend's Svix-signed webhook (`svix-id`/`svix-timestamp`/`svix-signature`) against the real `resend` SDK's runtime behavior, fails closed on any invalid signature, and is the only current writer of `source: 'inbound-webhook'` documents. This is a per-brand **dedicated mailbox address** model — zero rep setup required.
- **Existing periodic-job pattern**: `vercel.json` already declares three real Vercel Cron entries (`/api/admin/forecast-snapshot`, `/api/admin/ticket-size-recalc`, `/api/admin/cadence-tick`). `app/api/admin/cadence-tick/route.ts` demonstrates the established shape: `lib/api-auth.ts`'s `requireCronOrApiKey()` gates the route (fails closed in production if `SLG_API_KEY`/cron header isn't present), `app/lib/brand.ts`'s `getAllBrandConfigs()` iterates every configured brand, and a fixed per-run cap (`MAX_CADENCE_SENDS_PER_TICK = 200`) bounds each invocation so one busy brand can't starve another within a single serverless execution.
- **Admin human-review UI pattern**: `app/admin/duplicates/admin-duplicates-client.tsx` uses `AdminDataTable`/`AdminFormStatus`/`AdminResourceEmptyState` from `@sovereignsquad/gds-admin/client`, plus Mantine `Select`/`SegmentedControl`/`Button`, brand-scoped via `useAuth()`'s `brandLabels` — the established pattern this repo uses whenever a feature needs a rep/admin to review-then-apply rather than auto-apply.
- **Dependencies**: `package.json` (v2.4.188) currently has no Google API client library (`googleapis`, `google-auth-library`, or similar) anywhere in `dependencies`/`devDependencies` — this issue introduces the first one.

## 4. Problem Statement

Real lead-relevant email a rep sends/receives from their own Gmail — outside the brand's dedicated Resend address — never appears in this app's activity timeline, giving an incomplete picture of a lead's actual conversation history. Separately, a rep who already has a lead's contact saved in Google Contacts has no way to pull that person onto the lead record in this CRM except re-typing it by hand, risking drift from `contacts.ts`'s own established dedup/normalization rules if done outside the app's own write paths.

## 5. Goals

**Functional**
- Gmail messages to/from a lead's known contact addresses are ingested automatically (no rep action after connecting) and appear in the existing per-lead Activity tab, not a new/separate view.
- A rep can search their Google Contacts from a lead's detail view and attach a matched person as a new contact on that specific lead.

**Technical**
- Reuse `matchReplyToLeads`, `findMatchedContact`, and `generateContactSuggestion` (`lib/contact-reply-matching.ts`) unmodified for Gmail-sourced messages — no second matching implementation.
- Reuse `contactKey`, `dedupeContacts`, `deriveContactEmails` (`lib/contacts.ts`) unmodified for the Google Contacts import — no second dedup implementation.
- Add exactly one new `ActivitySource` value, `'gmail-sync'`, propagated consistently to every place that union is currently declared (`app/lib/activity-log-store.ts`, `app/components/ActivityPanel.tsx`).
- A well-defined, collision-resistant dedup key so the same physical email is never logged twice, including across the Resend and Gmail paths when both are active for the same brand.

**UX**
- Gmail-sourced entries render through the exact same `ActivityPanel` list, distinguishable by a labeled badge (not color alone).
- The Google Contacts import affordance follows this repo's established `/admin/duplicates`-style review-then-confirm pattern, not a silent background merge.
- No control implies a capability the rep hasn't actually connected (CLAUDE.md Rule 7) — an "Import from Google Contacts" action is disabled/hidden, never clickable-but-broken, when Google Contacts isn't connected.

## 6. Non-Goals

- **Real-time Gmail push sync** (Gmail API push notifications / Cloud Pub-Sub). v1 is periodic polling only — stated explicitly as a v1 simplification to avoid the added infrastructure (a Pub-Sub subscription, a public push endpoint, watch-renewal bookkeeping) this issue's scope doesn't justify.
- **Automatic, continuous, two-way Google Contacts sync.** v1 is a rep-initiated, one-way (Google → this app) import per contact. Continuous background sync has real conflict-resolution complexity (which side wins on a field disagreement, deletions, merges) that this repo's existing `/admin/duplicates` human-review pattern is a better fit for than an unattended job — not attempted here.
- **Sending email via Gmail.** That belongs to the separate "Outreach: One-off tracked email send" ticket's territory, which already sends via Resend. This issue does not add a second send path from a different identity.
- **Building the OAuth flow, token storage, or connection-management UI.** Entirely the sibling hub issue's scope; this issue only consumes a `getValidAccessToken(connectionId)`-shaped interface from it.
- **Google Calendar and Calendly.** Out of scope for this ticket (title-scoped to Gmail + Google Contacts only); tracked separately if/when picked up.

## 7. Mandatory Technical Constraints

### Design System Requirement (Mandatory)
All UI, UX, and design implementation must use only the Sovereign Squad General Design System (`@sovereignsquad/gds-core`/`gds-admin`/`gds-theme` `^6.5.0`, GitHub release tarballs, per `gds-adoption.json`). Any new sync-status/import UI must use GDS primitives or this repo's established Mantine usage pattern — no new component library.

- Brand/tenant scoping is mandatory on every new read/write, using the existing `resolveBrand()` (`app/lib/brand.ts`) and `getTenantId()`/`tenantFilter()` (`lib/tenant.ts`) helpers — no bespoke scoping logic.
- New periodic work is a Vercel Cron entry added to `vercel.json`, gated by `lib/api-auth.ts`'s `requireCronOrApiKey()`, following `app/api/admin/cadence-tick/route.ts`'s exact shape (per-run cap, per-brand loop via `getAllBrandConfigs()`).
- Any new direct npm dependency (a Google API client) must be checked for deprecation before being added, per CLAUDE.md Rule 1 — run and record the actual `npm view <pkg> deprecated` / install-time warning output, not an assumption.
- No parallel activity timeline, no parallel contact-dedup implementation — both are hard reuse requirements (Rule 5: never guess, verified against the real functions above).

## 8. Architecture

**Coexistence with the existing Resend inbound path (explicit decision):** Resend stays the **default, zero-setup** inbound path per brand's dedicated address. Gmail sync is an **opt-in addition**, not a replacement — a rep can have both active simultaneously for the same brand. Justification: Resend's dedicated address already guarantees every brand has inbound capture with no rep action; Gmail sync exists purely to *also* surface a rep's pre-existing personal-inbox activity for leads they already correspond with outside that address. Making them mutually exclusive would force a rep to give up the zero-setup path to opt into a personal one, which has no benefit. The corollary risk — the same physical email being visible to both paths for the same brand — is handled by the dedup key in §11, not by forcing exclusivity. Gmail sync is **read-only ingestion in v1**: it never sends from the rep's Gmail identity, avoiding two systems both capable of sending as the same brand/rep.

```
                         ┌─────────────────────────┐
 Resend dedicated addr → │ inbound-email webhook    │ → activityLog (source: 'inbound-webhook')
                         │ (issue #141, unchanged)  │
                         └─────────────────────────┘
                                                              \
                                                               ├─→ mergeActivityTimeline() → GET /api/leads/[id]/activity → ActivityPanel
                                                              /
 Rep's own Gmail inbox → ┌─────────────────────────┐
 (opt-in, polled)        │ Vercel Cron: gmail-sync  │ → activityLog (source: 'gmail-sync')
                         │ (this issue, new)        │
                         └─────────────────────────┘

 Rep's Google Contacts → ┌─────────────────────────┐
 (rep-initiated search)  │ Import-from-Contacts     │ → lead.contacts[] + contactEmails[]
                         │ action (this issue, new) │    (via the SAME write path every
                         └─────────────────────────┘     other contact write already uses)
```

Both new flows call into the hub issue's connection store only through a narrow interface this issue treats as a black box: `getValidAccessToken(connectionId): Promise<string | null>` (returns `null` when disconnected/unrefreshable — this issue never handles raw OAuth tokens, refresh logic, or credential storage itself).

## 9. Data Model/Contracts

- `app/lib/activity-log-store.ts`: extend `ActivitySource` to `'inbound-webhook' | 'manual' | 'outreach-log' | 'gmail-sync'`. No other field on `ActivityLogDocument`/`ActivityEntry` changes shape — `externalId` is reused (see §11 for its Gmail-specific value format), not duplicated.
- `app/components/ActivityPanel.tsx`: extend its local `ActivityEntry['source']` union identically, and add a `'Gmail'` badge label alongside the existing `TYPE_LABEL` map (badge text, not color alone, per §14).
- New collection `gmailSyncCursors`: `{ connectionId: string, brand: string, tenantId: string, lastSyncedAt: Date, lastHistoryId?: string, updatedAt: Date }` — one document per rep-connection-per-brand, indexed on `{ connectionId: 1, brand: 1 }` (unique). Purely an internal bookkeeping collection; never exposed via any API response.
- Google Contacts import introduces **no new persisted collection** — a successful import is a normal `contacts[]`/`contactEmails[]` write through the lead's existing write path.

## 10. API Contracts

- `POST /api/integrations/gmail/sync` — cron-triggered only (`requireCronOrApiKey`), no request body required, iterates every brand (`getAllBrandConfigs()`) and every Gmail-connected rep for that brand (via the hub's connection listing). Returns `{ processed: number, ingested: number, skipped: number, failures: Array<{ connectionId: string, reason: string }> }`, mirroring `cadence-tick`'s `TickSummary` shape. Never called directly by client UI.
- `GET /api/integrations/google-contacts/search?q=<query>&brand=<brand>` — rep-initiated, requires brand access (`requireBrandAccessApi`, same guard `GET /api/leads/[id]/activity` already uses). Returns a bounded list (cap: 25) of `{ resourceName: string, name: string, email?: string, phone?: string, organization?: string }`. Read-only against Google; never writes anything.
- `POST /api/leads/[id]/contacts/import-google` — body `{ resourceName: string }`, brand/tenant-scoped exactly like every other lead-mutating route. Executes the import algorithm in §11 and returns `{ status: 'added' | 'already-exists', contact: NormalizedContact }`. Idempotent: re-posting the same `resourceName` for the same lead after it was already added returns `already-exists`, never a duplicate.

## 11. Algorithm/Processing Logic

The title's "two-way ... data flow" is two distinct one-way ingestion flows (Gmail → activity timeline; Google Contacts → lead contacts), not bidirectional writes back into Gmail or Google Contacts — consistent with §6's explicit non-goals.

**Algorithm A — Gmail periodic poll + cross-source dedup** (runs once per connected rep, per cron tick):

```
function pollGmailForRep(rep, brand, tenantId):
    token = ConnectionHub.getValidAccessToken(rep.gmailConnectionId)
    if token is null:
        record failure "needs reauth" for this connectionId; return   # never aborts the whole cron run

    cursor = gmailSyncCursors.findOne({ connectionId: rep.gmailConnectionId, brand })
    # Safety net even with a cursor: never trust a stale/missing cursor to
    # justify an unbounded fetch — v1 always bounds to a recent window.
    windowStart = cursor?.lastSyncedAt ?? (now - 30 days)   # first-ever sync: 30-day window, not full mailbox history (stated v1 simplification)

    knownEmails = distinct contactEmails[] across every lead for (brand, tenantId)   # one indexed query, reused across every message in this poll

    headersOnly = GmailAPI.listMessageHeaders(token, since: windowStart, max: 50)   # headers-only call first — body is fetched only for a message that already matches
    newCursorMark = windowStart

    for msg in headersOnly (chronological):
        participantEmails = normalizeEmail(msg.from) ∪ normalizeEmail(each of msg.to, msg.cc)
        if participantEmails ∩ knownEmails is empty:
            continue     # not lead-related — never fetch this message's body, never store anything about it

        primaryDedupKey = "gmail:" + msg.messageIdHeader     # RFC 2822 Message-ID, globally unique per email
        if activityLog.exists({ externalId: primaryDedupKey }):
            continue     # already ingested — safe to re-run this poll

        # Cross-source guard: the same message may already be visible via
        # Resend's inbound-webhook path for the same brand when both are active.
        fallbackHash = sha256(normalizeEmail(msg.from) + "|" + sortedJoin(normalizeEmail(msg.to/cc)) + "|" + lower(trim(msg.subject)) + "|" + floorToMinute(msg.date))
        if activityLog.exists({ brand, source in ['inbound-webhook','gmail-sync'], fallbackHash: fallbackHash, createdAt within ±2min of msg.date }):
            continue     # same physical email already logged via the other path

        body = GmailAPI.getMessageBody(token, msg.id)   # fetched only now, only for a matched message
        direction = (normalizeEmail(msg.from) == rep.gmailAddress) ? 'outbound' : 'inbound'
        counterpartyEmail = direction == 'outbound' ? firstMatchOf(msg.to/cc, knownEmails) : msg.from

        matchResult = matchReplyToLeads(db, brand, tenantId, counterpartyEmail)   # UNCHANGED from issue #142
        leadId, matchedContactKey, matchedLeadIds = branch on matchResult.kind exactly as #141's webhook route already does

        insert ActivityLogDocument({
            leadId, tenantId, brand,
            type: direction == 'inbound' ? 'email-inbound' : 'email-outbound',
            direction, fromAddress: msg.from, toAddresses: msg.to, ccAddresses: msg.cc,
            subject: msg.subject, bodyExcerpt: truncateBody(body),   # UNCHANGED truncateBody(), 280 chars
            matchedContactKey, matchedLeadIds,
            source: 'gmail-sync', externalId: primaryDedupKey, fallbackHash,
            createdAt: msg.date,
        })

        if direction == 'inbound' and leadId:
            generateContactSuggestion(db, brand, tenantId, leadId, counterpartyEmail, body, insertedId)   # UNCHANGED from issue #142

        newCursorMark = max(newCursorMark, msg.date)

    gmailSyncCursors.upsert({ connectionId: rep.gmailConnectionId, brand }, { lastSyncedAt: newCursorMark, updatedAt: now })
    # Cursor only committed after the full batch succeeds — an aborted/failed
    # run (rep disconnects mid-poll, API error) leaves the prior cursor intact,
    # so the next run safely re-covers the same window rather than skipping it.
```

**Algorithm B — Google Contacts one-way import** (rep-initiated, synchronous):

```
function importGoogleContact(rep, leadId, brand, tenantId, resourceName):
    token = ConnectionHub.getValidAccessToken(rep.googleContactsConnectionId)
    if token is null: return 409 "Google Contacts not connected"

    person = PeopleAPI.getContact(token, resourceName)
    candidate = normalizeContact({               # UNCHANGED normalizeContact() from lib/contacts.ts
        name: person.name, title: person.organizationTitle,
        email: person.primaryEmail, phone: person.primaryPhone,
    })

    lead = loadLead(leadId, tenantId, brand)      # existing brand/tenant-scoped lookup, unchanged
    existing = dedupeContacts(lead.contacts)      # UNCHANGED dedupeContacts()
    key = contactKey(candidate)                   # UNCHANGED contactKey(): name+phone > name+email > bare name
    if key == '': return 400 "Contact needs at least a name"

    if existing.some(c => contactKey(c) == key):
        return { status: 'already-exists', contact: matchingExisting }   # no write — same identity, per contactKey()'s own definition

    lead.contacts.push(candidate)
    lead.contactEmails = deriveContactEmails(dedupeContacts(lead.contacts))   # UNCHANGED, kept in sync exactly like every other write path
    write lead via the SAME contact-write path PUT /api/leads/[id] already uses   # no new write logic
    return { status: 'added', contact: candidate }
```

## 12. Mathematical/Ranking Logic

N/A — this issue introduces no scoring, ranking, or weighting logic. Matching is exact-identifier (email/contactKey) throughout, reusing existing deterministic functions; no probabilistic or ranked output is produced.

## 13. UX/Operator Behaviour

- **Gmail sync**: fully passive from the rep's point of view once connected via the hub issue's settings UI — no ongoing action required. New entries simply appear in a lead's existing Activity tab (`ActivityPanel`) on next load, labeled with a `Gmail` badge distinct from `Inbound reply`/`Outbound email`.
- **Google Contacts import**: an "Import from Google Contacts" action on the lead detail view (near the existing Contacts section), visible/enabled only when the rep has an active Google Contacts connection (per Rule 7 — never a clickable-but-broken affordance when disconnected). Opens a search field; results render as a selectable list; picking one shows an inline "Already a contact on this lead" (no write) or "Add contact" confirmation before committing, following the same review-then-confirm spirit as `/admin/duplicates`.
- Errors (expired token, API quota, network failure) never crash the panel — same pattern `ActivityPanel.tsx`'s existing suggestions fetch already uses: a failed fetch degrades gracefully to an empty/error state, not a broken UI.

## 14. Accessibility Requirements (mandatory)

- Gmail-sourced activity entries are distinguished by a **text badge label** ("Gmail"), never color alone, matching WCAG 1.4.1 (use of color).
- The Google Contacts search results list is keyboard-navigable (arrow keys / Tab, Enter to select) and exposes results as a proper listbox (`role="listbox"`/`option` or GDS/Mantine's equivalent accessible pattern) with visible focus states.
- Search result count and add/already-exists outcomes are announced via an `aria-live="polite"` region, so a screen-reader user isn't left waiting on a silent async action.
- The "Import from Google Contacts" affordance's disabled state (when not connected) is exposed via `aria-disabled`/`disabled`, not merely styled to look inactive — consistent with Rule 7's affordance-matches-capability requirement applying equally to assistive tech, not just sighted users.
- All new interactive elements meet the same color-contrast and focus-visibility bar the rest of this app's Mantine/GDS-based UI already meets — no bespoke styling introduced.

## 15. Edge Cases

- Both Resend inbound and Gmail sync active for the same brand simultaneously — explicitly supported (§8); the fallback-hash cross-source guard (§11, Algorithm A) prevents the same physical email from appearing twice.
- A rep's OAuth token is expired/revoked mid-poll — that rep's batch is skipped with a recorded failure reason; the cron run continues for every other rep/brand in the same invocation (same "don't let one failure block the batch" precedent `cadence-tick`'s per-brand loop already follows).
- A Gmail message with no `Message-ID` header (rare, malformed/very old mail) — falls back to the hash-based dedup key alone; documented as a known, low-probability v1 limitation, not silently ignored.
- A lead's contact email changes or is removed after Gmail messages were already ingested against it — historical `activityLog` entries keep their original `matchedContactKey`/`leadId` (no retroactive re-matching), identical to the existing Resend-sourced behavior — no new precedent invented.
- Rep disconnects Gmail mid-poll-cycle — the sync cursor is only committed after the full batch succeeds (§11), so a partial/aborted run never corrupts the resume point.
- Multi-match (the same contact email listed on more than one lead) — handled identically to `matchReplyToLeads`'s existing multi-match branch; no new behavior.
- Google Contacts search result has no email/phone (name-only) — `contactKey()` falls back to bare name (existing behavior); the import UI surfaces a "weaker match, review before adding" notice rather than silently treating it the same as an email/phone-backed contact.
- First-ever sync for a newly-connected rep with no cursor — bounded to a 30-day window, never a full historical mailbox backfill (stated v1 simplification, §11).
- Rep's Gmail address itself appears in `contactEmails[]` by coincidence (e.g. they added themselves as a contact by mistake) — out of scope to specially detect; treated the same as any other match, since preventing this is a data-quality issue in `contacts[]`, not a sync-logic concern.

## 16. Performance Expectations

- Poll cadence: every 15–30 minutes via a new `vercel.json` cron entry (final cadence decided at implementation time against Vercel Cron's actual minimum-interval limits for this project's plan) — never real-time (§6).
- Each cron invocation processes brands via `getAllBrandConfigs()` and reps within a bounded per-run cap (mirroring `MAX_CADENCE_SENDS_PER_TICK`'s precedent) so one busy brand/rep can't exhaust a single serverless function's time/memory budget.
- Per-message cost is minimized by a headers-only Gmail API call first; a message body is fetched only after it has already matched `contactEmails[]` — bounds both API quota usage and how much of a rep's unrelated personal mail is ever touched.
- The `contactEmails[]` intersection check is one indexed query per brand/tenant per poll, not a per-message database round-trip.
- Google Contacts search is rep-initiated and synchronous — target p95 response time under 2 seconds, consistent with a live search-as-you-type interaction rather than a batch operation.

## 17. Security/Privacy Requirements (mandatory)

This touches a rep's real personal Gmail inbox and real third-party PII (lead contacts) — scope minimization is the central constraint throughout, not an afterthought:

- **Minimum OAuth scopes**: Gmail — `gmail.readonly` only (never `gmail.modify`, `gmail.send`, or full-mailbox scopes; this issue never sends or mutates the rep's mailbox). Google Contacts — `contacts.readonly` only (never the read-write `contacts` scope; v1 never writes back to Google Contacts, per §6).
- **No token handling in this issue**: OAuth tokens are stored, refreshed, and retrieved exclusively through the sibling hub issue's credential store, accessed only via the narrow `getValidAccessToken(connectionId)` interface (§8). This issue's own code never persists a raw access/refresh token.
- **Data-minimization by construction**: the headers-only-then-body-on-match fetch order (§16) means a rep's unrelated personal correspondence is never even fetched into this app's process, let alone stored — only messages whose participants intersect a lead's own `contactEmails[]` are ever touched past the header stage.
- **Body storage is already bounded**: reused `truncateBody()` (`activity-log-store.ts`, 280-char cap) — full email bodies are never persisted, exactly as the existing Resend-sourced entries already behave; this is not a new decision introduced by this issue.
- **Strict brand/tenant isolation**: every read/write goes through the existing `resolveBrand()`/`tenantFilter()` helpers — a rep's Gmail data ingested under one brand's context must never cross-write into another brand/tenant's `activityLog`.
- **Revocation behavior, stated explicitly**: disconnecting Gmail or Google Contacts (owned by the hub issue's UI) immediately stops future polls/imports for that connection. Already-ingested `activityLog` entries are **not** retroactively deleted — this matches how disabling the Resend webhook doesn't purge past inbound activity, and is called out here as an intentional, consistent choice rather than an oversight.
- **No credential or token values in logs**, ever — matching this repo's existing discipline (`activity-log-store.ts`/`contacts.ts` log only structural error context, never payload contents).
- **Rate limiting/backoff**: Gmail API and People API quota errors are caught and backed off per-connection, never allowed to fail an entire cron invocation for every other rep.

## 18. Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ActivitySource` (both `app/lib/activity-log-store.ts` and `app/components/ActivityPanel.tsx`) includes `'gmail-sync'`, consistently, with no type mismatch between server and client.
- [ ] A real Gmail message from/to an address present in a brand's `contactEmails[]` is ingested into `activityLog` with `source: 'gmail-sync'`, correct `leadId`/`matchedContactKey` (via unmodified `matchReplyToLeads`/`findMatchedContact`), and appears in `GET /api/leads/[id]/activity`'s merged response and in `ActivityPanel`.
- [ ] A Gmail message from an address not in any lead's `contactEmails[]` is never fetched past the headers stage and never stored.
- [ ] Re-running the poll for the same time window never produces a duplicate `activityLog` entry (verified against `externalId`).
- [ ] When both Resend and Gmail sync are active for the same brand and see the same physical email, only one `activityLog` entry results (fallback-hash guard verified).
- [ ] An inbound Gmail-sourced reply with a changed signature-block detail produces a pending `contactSuggestions` entry via unmodified `generateContactSuggestion()`, never an automatic `contacts[]` write.
- [ ] `POST /api/leads/[id]/contacts/import-google` adds a new contact via the existing write path, keeps `contactEmails[]` in sync, and returns `already-exists` (no duplicate write) on a repeat import of the same person.
- [ ] The "Import from Google Contacts" action is disabled/hidden (not merely styled inactive) when the rep has no active Google Contacts connection.
- [ ] An expired/revoked token for one rep does not prevent the same cron run from processing every other connected rep.

## 19. Testing Requirements

- **Unit tests**: dedup-key generation (`externalId`, `fallbackHash`) for representative message shapes; the cross-source dedup guard's window/match logic; the `contactKey()`-based already-exists branch in Algorithm B; the headers-only-then-body-on-match gating logic (asserting a body fetch is never issued for a non-matching message).
- **Integration tests**: a simulated Gmail poll cycle against a mocked Gmail/People API and `mongodb-memory-server` (already a devDependency) producing correct `activityLog` entries, with the same poll run twice producing no duplicates; a simulated `import-google` call verifying the resulting `contacts[]`/`contactEmails[]` state matches every other write path's invariants.
- **Manual verification** (documented, per CLAUDE.md Rule 4): at least one real end-to-end run against a real test Gmail account and a real Google Contacts entry, before this ships, with the actual output recorded — not inferred.
- Full CLAUDE.md Rule 1 gate: `npx tsc --noEmit` zero errors, `npm run lint` zero errors/zero warnings in touched files, `npx vitest run` and the smoke suite (`npm run test:smoke`) 100% passing, `npm run audit:gds-style` clean for any new UI.

## 20. Documentation Requirements

- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: document the Gmail-sync and Google-Contacts-import flows, the coexistence decision with Resend (§8), and the dedup-key design (§11).
- `docs/OPERATOR_GUIDE.md`: document how a rep connects Gmail/Contacts (pointing to the hub issue's connection UI) and how to use the "Import from Google Contacts" action.
- `README.md` and/or environment-variable documentation: any new required configuration this issue itself introduces (e.g. the cron schedule entry in `vercel.json`), distinct from the OAuth client credentials themselves (owned by the hub issue).
- `CHANGELOG.md` + version bump, per this repo's existing convention.
- Any newly-added direct dependency's deprecation-check result (per §7) recorded in the commit/PR description, even if the result is "clean."

## 21. Handover Requirements

- Rollback for Gmail sync: disable the `vercel.json` cron entry (or flip a feature flag if one is added at implementation time) — stops all future polling immediately; no destructive action needed, `activityLog` data already written is left as-is (consistent with §17's revocation behavior).
- Rollback for Google Contacts import: remove/disable the UI action and the `import-google` route — no background job to stop, since imports are synchronous and rep-initiated only.
- No production data is touched destructively by either flow: Gmail sync only inserts new `activityLog` documents (never updates/deletes existing ones); Contacts import only appends to `contacts[]` via the same reviewed write path every other contact addition already uses.
- This issue introduces no new auth/session model — it consumes the hub issue's connection store as a black box; a handover reader only needs to understand the `getValidAccessToken(connectionId)` contract, not any OAuth internals (those live in the hub issue).

## 22. Delivery Expectations (CLAUDE.md zero-tolerance gate)

Per CLAUDE.md Rule 1, nothing in this issue's implementation reaches `main` with: any `tsc --noEmit` error; any lint error, or any lint warning in a touched file; a failing `vitest run` or smoke-suite test; an undisclosed newly-added direct dependency deprecation. If a new Google API client dependency's deprecation status, or its own transitive deprecation warnings, can't be fully resolved within this issue's scope, that must be stated explicitly in the PR/commit description with a one-line reason, per Rule 1 — never silently shipped unmentioned.

## 23. Final Rule

If implementing this to the full standard above (in particular, achieving a genuinely zero-warning, zero-deprecation dependency addition, or building out the full accessibility surface in §14) turns out to require more scope than this single issue reasonably covers, that must be said explicitly and split into its own separately-tracked follow-up issue — never silently under-delivered against this issue's own Acceptance Criteria.

## 24. Dependencies/Execution Order

- **Depends on**: "Integrations: Third-party connection hub - admin-managed credentials for Google Workspace and Calendly" (sibling issue, filed in the same batch as this one) — this issue's `getValidAccessToken(connectionId)` interface and all Google OAuth scopes/consent flow are that issue's deliverable, not this one's. Implementation of this issue should not begin until that interface's contract is at least defined, even if its full UI isn't finished.
- **Builds on** (already shipped, no changes required to their own logic): #140 (`activityLog`/`ActivityPanel`), #141 (Resend inbound webhook — coexistence partner, §8), #142 (`contact-reply-matching.ts` — reused unmodified), and `lib/contacts.ts`'s contact-normalization module (reused unmodified).
- **Explicitly non-blocking, in either direction**, with the "Outreach: One-off tracked email send" ticket — that issue sends via Resend; this issue is read-only ingestion via Gmail; different code paths, no shared state, no ordering requirement between them (§6).

items.body:
## Functional deliverable — minimum safe Capsule handoff (G2–G3)

**Goal:** Make the existing Capsule Release wizard's already approved/accepted Tenant handoff **actually work**. Stop building standalone proof frameworks.

### Deliver in this issue
- Connect the existing current preflight/approved plan and explicit Platform Admin successor acceptance to ONE guarded runtime handoff path. Use existing components rather than another architecture layer.
- At the moment of operation, verify current Capsule/Namespace/resource UID, RV, ownership/consent and sufficient provider authority; keep v1beta2 Capsule CR/spec, quota/limit policy, workloads, provider-owned objects and foreign RBAC unchanged.
- Perform server `dryRun=All` for the exact **KAORI metadata-only** candidates, then a separately authorized conditional PATCH and complete authoritative read-back, with a durable START attempt recorded before any mutation.
- Report **success / still pending / partial or unknown**. A partial/unknown result blocks Released, supplies a focused manual recovery action and is never auto-retried.

### Exit criteria
**Function complete** only when real path is wired and authorized regression/UAT proves one successful exact-scope handoff plus rejection of stale UID/RV, unsafe ownership/policy change and partial outcome. Source-only hash correlation or a merged PR is **not** PASS.

### Explicitly defer to separate review/audit backlog
New audit-envelope formats, duplicate provenance frameworks, speculative IdP/Vault resolver implementations, additional nonessential tables and exhaustive edge-case matrices **unless a specific test demonstrates they are required to keep this path safe**. Existing relevant contracts/fixtures should be reused or simplified.

**Next:** #1230 finalizer → #1231 Re-Adopt/UAT. #1229 remains OPEN. **HOLD:** tests/CI/CD/DevContainer QA, migration/SQL operational writes, Kubernetes/Vault/IdP/live provider operations, Release, deployment or staging/main promotion require separate operator approval; only source PRs to `kaori/review/staging-uat` are currently allowed. Existing START/proof writers remain disabled until that authorization.

items.title: Divorce SLA management from prioritisation beyond creation
items.body:
# CMS SLA management - priority and SLA model

The design for case prioritisation and SLA tracking in the CMS.
This doc is the settled replacement for the broken `Priority` enum (`NEW / URGENT / CRITICAL / BREACH`),
which conflated two orthogonal concepts - inherent severity and time-derived SLA progress - into one field that a background job continuously overwrote.

Part of the CMS doc set:

- [dashboard-data-queries.md](dashboard-data-queries.md) - Dashboard (shared mechanics)
- [case-status-report-analysis.md](case-status-report-analysis.md)
- [case-ageing-report-analysis.md](case-ageing-report-analysis.md)
- [cms-statemachine-diagram.md](cms-statemachine-diagram.md) - case lifecycle / status set
- cms-sla-management.md (this doc)

[PDF links here](https://github.com/tazama-lf/case-management-system/issues/218#issuecomment-4832571623)

## 1. The problem being replaced

The current `Priority` enum is an SLA-urgency ladder masquerading as a priority:

- `enum Priority { NEW, URGENT, CRITICAL, BREACH }` ([schema.prisma](tazama-lf/case-management-system/backend/prisma/schema.prisma#L241)), used by `Alert.priority` and `Case.priority`.
- Both [case-priority.util.ts](tazama-lf/case-management-system/backend/src/modules/shared/utils/case-priority.util.ts) `determinePriority(score)` and [alert-priority.service.ts](tazama-lf/case-management-system/backend/src/modules/alert-priority/alert-priority.service.ts) map a `0..1` score onto the enum with the same thresholds (`>= 1.0 -> BREACH`, `>= 0.66 -> CRITICAL`, `>= 0.33 -> URGENT`, else `NEW`).
- In the alert service that score **is** `slaProgress = elapsedHours / DEFAULT_SLA_HOURS` (72h). So `NEW` = fresh, `URGENT` = past 1/3 of SLA, `CRITICAL` = past 2/3, `BREACH` = SLA exceeded.
- The recalculation job (`runRecalculation`) **overwrites** `case.priority` every cycle from this SLA progress, so the field can never hold a stable human- or rule-set priority. This is the original sin: a derived time-state clobbering a severity value.

Two distinct questions had been crushed into one field:

- **How serious is this case?** (inherent severity - stable, set by triage)
- **How is this case tracking against its clock?** (time-derived - changes every tick)

This doc separates them into two orthogonal axes.

## 2. The two axes

| Axis | Field | Meaning | Set by | Mutates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Priority (severity) | `priority` | How serious the case inherently is | Triage, from `priorityScore` | Only by explicit, audited actuation (section 8) |
| SLA state (timing) | `sla_state` (derived) | How the case is tracking against its deadline | Derived from `now` vs `sla_due_at` | Continuously, as a pure function of time |

They are a **matrix**, not a single ladder: a `HIGH` case can be `ON_TRACK`, and a `LOW` case can be `BREACHED`.
Priority does not move because the clock moved; SLA state does not move because severity was reassessed (except via the deadline it implies, section 8).

## 3. Priority - the severity axis

```
enum Priority { LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH }
```

- `NEW` disappears entirely. "The clock has started" is a timestamp fact (`created_at`), not a priority value - it was part of the original conflation.
- `BREACH` disappears from this axis - it is an SLA state, not a severity (section 4).
- Stamped once at triage from the existing `priorityScore` by a repurposed `determinePriority(score)` that now returns a 3-bucket severity (`LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH`) instead of the SLA ladder.
- **Never written by the SLA job.** The recalc job stops touching `priority` - that removes the original sin.
- Mutable only through an explicit, audited actuator over the case lifecycle (section 8).

## 4. SLA state - the timing axis

```
sla_state in { ON_TRACK, AT_RISK, DUE_SOON, BREACHED }   // derived, not stored canonically
```

Four states, because the run-up drives **two distinct escalation actions** (section 7), so `AT_RISK` and `DUE_SOON` each earn their place:

| sla_state | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| ON_TRACK | within the early part of the SLA budget |
| AT_RISK | past the at-risk milestone - first escalation trigger |
| DUE_SOON | past the due-soon milestone - second, different escalation trigger |
| BREACHED | SLA budget exceeded |

`OVERDUE` and `BREACHED` collapse into a single `BREACHED` value (they were two names for "past the deadline").
`APPROACHING` is named `AT_RISK` (industry-standard phrasing).

`sla_state` is a **pure function of `now` vs the case's deadline** and is derived on read (section 6) - it is never stored as canonical state, so it can never go stale.

## 5. Priority parameterises the SLA clock

Priority does not just sit alongside SLA state for display - it **calibrates the clock**.
This is the standard severity-drives-SLA-target model (Jira / ServiceNow / Zendesk all key SLA targets off priority).

```
priority           -> slaTarget(tenant, priority)         // hours, from tenant policy
elapsed / target   -> slaProgress
bucket(slaProgress, breakpoints(tenant, priority)) -> sla_state
```

Each priority has its own SLA budget (`HIGH` short, `LOW` long), so the `ON_TRACK / AT_RISK / DUE_SOON` milestones are appropriately scaled per severity.
This resolves the "a fresh case stays fresh for too long" complaint: a `HIGH` case burns through its run-up far faster than a `LOW` one.

### MVP: shared breakpoints x per-priority targets

The breakpoint **percentages** are shared across priorities (e.g. `AT_RISK` at 50%, `DUE_SOON` at 80%, `BREACHED` at 100%); only the **absolute target** varies by priority.
The shape of the run-up is constant; the timeline length differs because the budget differs.

| priority | target (illustrative default) | AT_RISK at | DUE_SOON at | BREACHED at |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HIGH | 24h | 12h | 19.2h | 24h |
| MEDIUM | 72h | 36h | 57.6h | 72h |
| LOW | 168h (7d) | 84h | 134.4h | 168h |

> Targets above are illustrative only - the real numbers are tenant configuration (section 9), not fixed constants.

### Keeping the future change cheap

A later move to **per-priority breakpoints** (e.g. `HIGH` warns proportionally earlier, not just absolutely earlier) must have a small blast radius.
That is guaranteed structurally by resolving the breakpoints **through the policy, keyed by priority, from day one** - even though MVP seeds identical percentages for all three priorities:

```
determineSlaState(elapsedHours, priority, slaPolicy) -> sla_state
  target   = slaPolicy.targetHours[priority]
  atRisk   = slaPolicy.breakpoints[priority].atRisk    // MVP: same value for all 3
  dueSoon  = slaPolicy.breakpoints[priority].dueSoon   // MVP: same value for all 3
  progress = elapsedHours / target
  if progress >= 1.0      -> BREACHED
  else if progress >= dueSoon -> DUE_SOON
  else if progress >= atRisk  -> AT_RISK
  else                        -> ON_TRACK
```

The function signature and every call site already take priority and resolve per-priority breakpoints.
The day per-priority breakpoints are wanted, the change is a **config-data edit only** - no code, no migration, no call-site churn.

## 6. The deadline: freeze at creation, derive state on read

Store the **deadline**, not the state.

- At creation (and on any priority change, section 8), compute and persist:

  `sla_due_at = created_at + slaTarget(tenant, priority)`

- Derive `sla_state` at read time from `now` vs `sla_due_at`. It is never stale, needs no job to stay current, and yields a free countdown ("due in 6h") the UI can show and sort by.
- `sla_due_at` moves only when its inputs move: a priority change (section 8) or - by explicit admin action only - a tenant policy re-stamp (section 9).

The SLA job therefore writes **no canonical state**. Its only remaining job is firing escalations (section 7).

This fully separates the three concerns the old enum had crushed together:

- **priority** - severity, set once, audited changes only
- **sla_due_at / sla_state** - derived timing, never overwritten by a job
- **escalation** - side effects, an idempotent job

## 7. Escalation - keyed on `(sla_state x ownership)`

The escalation decision is a function of **two** axes: the SLA state and whether the case has an owner.
The enum stays small; escalation is a policy layer on top of it (do not encode "unclaimed" or "escalated" into the SLA state).

| sla_state | unowned (claimable pool) | owned |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ON_TRACK | normal queue, no action | no action |
| AT_RISK | **escalate: at risk, nobody has picked it up** | owner nudge (optional) |
| DUE_SOON | escalate: unclaimed and due soon | **escalate: owner may need support to avoid breach** |
| BREACHED | escalate: breached, unclaimed | escalate: breached |

The two bolded cells are the user-confirmed distinct triggers - a *claim*-chase (`AT_RISK` + unowned) and a *support*-chase (`DUE_SOON` + owned) - which is why four states are warranted rather than three.

"Unowned" here is the same claimable-pool concept (unassigned / ready-for-assignment) that the reports work splits out of an individual investigator's backlog - same seam, reused.

The escalation job:

- reads `(sla_state, has_owner)` per open case and fires the matching notification;
- writes no canonical state;
- is **idempotent**: it records which `(case_id, sla_state)` notifications it has already sent, so a case is not re-notified every tick. A genuine state change (including one caused by a priority change, section 8) is a new `(case_id, sla_state)` pair and so fires a fresh, correctly-reasoned escalation.

## 8. Changing priority during the case lifecycle

Priority is mutable - new evidence can make a `MEDIUM` case `HIGH`, or downgrade one - but it changes **only through an explicit, audited actuator**, never through the SLA job.

### Rule: re-anchor the deadline on `created_at`, not on `now`

On a change from `p_old` to `p_new`:

`sla_due_at := created_at + slaTarget(tenant, p_new)`

The clock is **not** reset - only the budget changes.
Elapsed time already accrued counts against the new budget; `sla_state` is then re-derived on the next read from `now` vs the new `sla_due_at`.

### Why anchor on `created_at` (the non-gameable choice)

| Option | Behaviour | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Re-anchor on `created_at`** (chosen) | `due_at = created_at + target(p_new)` | An SLA is a commitment from when the case began. A case now recognised as `HIGH` and already old genuinely *is* in trouble and should reflect that immediately. Honest, non-gameable. |
| Reset to `now` | `due_at = now + target(p_new)` | Restarts the clock - a near-breach case buys a fresh full budget just by re-prioritising. Gameable; hides real ageing. Rejected. |
| Proportional / preserve consumed fraction | carry the used fraction across budgets | Clever but hard to explain to an auditor ("why is the deadline 3.2 days when HIGH is 1 day?"); over-engineered for MVP. Rejected. |

### Consequences (all intended)

- **Escalation up** (`MEDIUM -> HIGH`) shortens the budget. The case may jump straight to `AT_RISK / DUE_SOON / BREACHED` and escalate immediately. That is exactly the wanted signal: urgent and already old means escalate now.
- **De-escalation** (`HIGH -> LOW`) lengthens the budget and may move a case back from `BREACHED` to a run-up state. Because `sla_state` is derived, it can move backwards.
- **Immediate, correct escalation:** the re-stamp changes `sla_state`, which is a new `(case_id, sla_state)` pair, so the idempotent job fires a fresh escalation rather than suppressing it as already-sent.

### Audit

- Every priority change is a discrete domain event (`PriorityChanged`) recording **actor, timestamp, old priority, new priority, and reason** on the case timeline - because it moves a contractual SLA commitment.
- The event triggers the `sla_due_at` re-stamp; the SLA job remains a pure reader.
- Authorisation: priority changes are a supervisor/admin action (or a deliberate re-scoring event), consistent with the rest of the case-action model.

### Reconciling with "set once at triage, never overwritten"

- "Never overwritten" applies to the **SLA recalc job** - it must never write `priority` (removing the original sin).
- The **initial** value is stamped at triage from `priorityScore`.
- Thereafter priority moves **only** through the explicit actuator above - a manual supervisor change or a deliberate re-score event - not a continuous background overwrite. (A future auto-re-score must go through this same audited actuator, never become a per-tick clobber.)

## 9. Tenant configuration

SLA targets are **per-tenant** and contractually negotiated: an operator may run a managed service for several tenants, each with its own negotiated SLAs.
The policy is therefore **data, not environment** (env cannot vary per tenant).

Policy shape (per tenant, per priority):

| Field | Example |
| --- | --- |
| `tenant_id` | (FK) |
| `priority` | LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH |
| `target_hours` | 168 / 72 / 24 |
| `at_risk_pct` | 0.5 |
| `due_soon_pct` | 0.8 |

Resolution chain (so an unconfigured tenant is still safe):

```
tenant + priority row  ->  system default per priority  ->  hard-coded floor
```

- The **system default** lives in env / config (the fallback when a tenant has no row).
- The **per-tenant overrides** live in the DB. Onboarding a new contract is a data insert, not a deploy.
- A tenant-policy change applies to **new** cases only by default (deadlines are frozen at creation, section 6). An explicit, opt-in admin "re-stamp open cases" action exists for the rare case where a renegotiation must apply retroactively - it is never the silent default.

## 10. Settled model - summary

- `priority = LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH`, stamped once at triage from `priorityScore`, never written by the SLA job.
- `sla_due_at` stamped at creation from the **tenant** policy; re-anchored on `created_at` (not `now`) on any audited priority change.
- `sla_state = ON_TRACK / AT_RISK / DUE_SOON / BREACHED`, derived on read from `now` vs `sla_due_at` - never stored as canonical state.
- breakpoints resolved per-priority through the policy from day one; MVP seeds them equal (shared % x per-priority targets).
- escalation keyed on `(sla_state x ownership)`; the job fires notifications only and is idempotent.
- the old recalc job stops writing `priority` entirely.

## 11. Implementation surface (from the blast-radius assessment)

Three files define 100% of the broken semantics today and are the core of the change:

- [case-priority.util.ts](tazama-lf/case-management-system/backend/src/modules/shared/utils/case-priority.util.ts) - `determinePriority` becomes a 3-bucket severity mapper (`LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH`).
- [alert-priority.service.ts](tazama-lf/case-management-system/backend/src/modules/alert-priority/alert-priority.service.ts) - the recalc job stops writing `priority`; it derives `sla_state` for escalation only and is fed a per-priority, per-tenant target instead of the single `DEFAULT_SLA_HOURS`.
- [schema.prisma](tazama-lf/case-management-system/backend/prisma/schema.prisma#L241) - `Priority` enum becomes `LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH`; add `sla_due_at`; add the tenant SLA-policy model.

Wider touch points (counts from the assessment): ~42 non-test source files and ~14 test/fixture files reference `Priority`; three competing priority vocabularies already exist in the tree and must converge on `LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH`. The DB change is a schema split plus a per-tenant data backfill, not a 1:1 enum rename.

## 12. Open items (deferred, not pre-built)

- **Sticky "was-breached" audit flag.** `sla_state` is derived and can move backwards on de-escalation. If audit needs an immutable "ever breached" fact, that is a separate sticky boolean set once and never cleared - explicitly deferred, not built into the SLA state.
- **Per-priority breakpoints.** Structurally ready (section 5) but seeded equal in MVP; promote only with a concrete reason for a priority to warn proportionally earlier.
- **Automatic re-scoring of priority.** Possible later, but must flow through the audited `PriorityChanged` actuator (section 8), never re-introduce a per-tick overwrite.
- **Severity-bucket thresholds** (the `priorityScore -> LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH` cut points) could themselves become tenant config; MVP keeps a shared default.

items.title: Complete Dashboard API v1 parity and migrate dashboard to shared JSON contract for WebOS/Android
items.body:
## Goal
Complete the existing `/api/v1` as the canonical read-only representation of everything available in the Reports dashboard, then make the HTML/htmx dashboard consume the same shared application/service contract. Future WebOS/Android clients are **out of scope**.

## Existing baseline (avoid duplication)
- `src/ocpp_reports/api_v1.py` already exposes `/api/v1/summary`, `/connectors`, `/transactions`, `/stations`, `/filters`, `/openapi.json`, registered by `web.py`.
- `web.py` also exposes legacy `/api/snapshot`, `/api/event-group`, and HTML transaction detail. These are existing routes; prior Reports HTTP contracts are not a compatibility requirement after coordinated fleet upgrade.
- Current v1 has incomplete parity: transactions only support view/page with hardcoded empty term/status/location/date and UTC; no JSON transaction detail, event group/history, source synchronization/freshness, timezone options, or complete dashboard filter/view semantics. Current dashboard still assembles HTML data via `read` rather than consuming the v1 contract.
- Preserve existing login/auth middleware, source allowlists, admin/operator/customer separation, tenant isolation and no-write behavior. Coordinate with #111, #114, #162, #185/#188 rather than duplicating their fixes.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Inventory all dashboard panels and fields (status summary, connectors/station 0/individual, source/station/location filters, transaction list/details, event groups, active energy, power, SoC, synchronization and provenance/freshness, timestamps and selectable timezones). Record field-to-endpoint parity matrix and unknown/unavailable semantics.
2. Versioned JSON schemas with stable pagination, validation, timestamps, timezone behavior, explicit nulls, error handling, OpenAPI examples; reuse existing warehouse projections and business rules (no second business logic).
3. Tenant and role-scoped authorization on **every** endpoint, including ID enumeration, details, filters, pagination, event history; reject cross-tenant requests, no information leakage, no unsafe CORS or unauthenticated fallback.
4. Dashboard and API use one application service/query layer; migrate dashboard without breaking HTML, htmx refresh/scroll, login/profile/password, current supported URLs. Preserve p95 <1s benchmark target.
5. Automated parity tests (HTML vs JSON for identical filters), negative auth/tenant tests, rebuild-from-forwarders verification (cursor-zero replay, counts, transaction/event evidence) and empty data tests, timezone/DST, energy/status aggregation and pagination, OpenAPI contract tests.
6. CI green, review and merge incremental PRs; deploy through the existing idempotent Ansible pipeline once, verify live API/dashboard and document acceptance. Follow the repository FIX-FORWARD policy: correct defects with a subsequent tested commit/deployment; preserve historical source SQLite evidence and rebuild Collector from retained Forwarder journals; old Reports binaries, prior HTTP contracts and unsupported export schemas need not remain compatible. Rollback, version reversal and Ansible compensations are not acceptance criteria. No WebOS/Android UI implementation.

## Upgrade scope
All Reports installations will be upgraded to the new version. No backwards compatibility requirement for old Reports releases or retired HTTP endpoints. Verify the supported current producer export schema separately; do not retain `ocpp-csms/export/v1` solely for compatibility unless it remains a supported input. Preserve Forwarder source SQLite evidence. Rebuild the Collector from a new empty database by replaying its complete retained local replication journals, verifying per-source cursors, counts and evidence. Collector schema migration is not mandatory when rebuild succeeds; do not delete old Collector before acceptance. This is a coordinated FIX-FORWARD upgrade.

## Suggested increments
A. Extract shared dashboard query/projection layer + parity inventory; B. complete v1 endpoints/filters/detail and schemas; C. migrate HTML/htmx to shared contract; D. auth/performance regression, deploy and field validation.

Do not close until deployed API and dashboard are verified against the same data and source-scoped identities.

## Collector rebuild acceptance (preproduction, November 2026)
- Audit retention/purge paths and confirm each Forwarder local `replication_changes` journal can be replayed from sequence zero. Absence of manual purges alone is not sufficient proof.
- Validate isolated new Collector ingest with paginated journal replay, matching source-specific event/transaction/rating/connector evidence, last sequence, and idempotent retries.
- **Current forwarder state is monotonic:** `forward_cursors` persists acknowledgments and `save_cursor` refuses regressions. A new Collector at cursor zero cannot be repopulated by an unchanged running Forwarder with an advanced cursor. Design and test an explicitly authorized, bounded replay/reseed mechanism before any real cutover; do not mutate production cursors during CI.
- Retain old Collector and all Forwarder databases until reconstruction has passed and been explicitly approved. No automatic rollback or Ansible compensation.
- A partial retained history must be reported as partial, not silently labeled complete. No compatibility requirement for old Reports releases or retired HTTP contracts.

items.title: benchmarking: Benchmark system map + enforced preflight manifest
items.body:
## Summary

Create a benchmark system map documenting the full stack and signal activation state, plus an enforced preflight manifest that prevents benchmark runs when the deployment doesn't match expectations.

## Design reference

- Findings from #369 (baseline discrepancy investigation)

## Scope

### 1. `docs/benchmark-system-map.md`

- Stack diagram: AMB harness -> EvalHub adapter -> EvalHub server/sidecar/MLflow -> MCP server -> `search_memories_with_focus` -> corpus (tenant/schema)
- **Signal activation matrix** -- one row per RRF signal:

  | signal | implemented where | activation prerequisite | verify-active command | active in deployment today? |

  Rows: vector, reranker (TEI URL, #342), keyword (index + query path), focus (set_focus session state), domain (tags on corpus), graph (relationship edges). Fill "today?" from live checks, not memory.
- Corpus provenance section: which corpora exist in which tenants, what produced them, chunked or raw.

### 2. `benchmarks/preflight.py`

- Emits manifest JSON: per-signal active/inactive (reranker URL reachable, tsvector index present + used, domain-tag count, edge count, focus state), corpus provenance (tenant, node count, chunk count, ingestion label), k, answer model, pipeline/SDK/adapter SHAs.
- Benchmark configs declare `expected_manifest` (subset match). Harness/adapter REFUSES to run on mismatch (hard fail, printed diff).
- Manifest embedded in results metadata and MLflow tags.

## Exit predicate

Preflight runs against mcp-rhoai and prints a manifest matching #369's findings; a deliberately wrong expectation (e.g. `reranker: active` today) fails the run with a readable diff; all matrix config files carry `expected_manifest`.

## Verifier

The deliberate-mismatch test; manifest visible in a smoke run's MLflow tags.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by #369 (map records its findings; preflight asserts them)

items.title: RFC: MCP Apps (SEP-1865) host support in ADK Python — stable-subset host seam: dual-era advertisement, catalog policy, render bootstrap, governed app invocations
items.body:
> **Revision 4.19 (2026-08-13) — upstream-draft revision, resolving the four P0 blockers and four P1 corrections from the [Revision 4.18 review](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/BigQuery-Agent-Analytics-SDK/issues/406#issuecomment-5277329397).** Changes: every operation gets a **progress-delivery gate** (terminal response atomically closes intake and **drains admitted progress callbacks before result approval, ledger freeze, Event append, and Runner-loop release**); batch discovery becomes a **class-neutral deterministic two-class algorithm** (app-safe listing first; explicit same-name disagreement rule; UI/non-UI disagreement fails closed — never silent reuse of a stale class); the refresh record becomes the exact **`RefreshInvocationRecord`** — a purpose-separated record inside the same opaque sidecar envelope reached by `sealedResultRef`, with immutable-create keys, envelope-before-append write ordering, crash recovery, GC, and incarnation-cascade deletion; and **export gains its matrix row, a through-release permit (streaming prohibited in v1), and a named audit-store contract** in the host profile (a sixth deployment contract), with the durable row honestly described as an authorization/release-attempt record, not delivery proof. P1 corrections: the superseded §1 cleanup paragraph is replaced by the lease-token model, the byte-identity claim is scoped to non-UI paths, ratification 7(k)'s labels now match the adopted per-Session default, and the fixture version, PR contents, and provider count are synchronized. **Per the 4.18 review's presentation guidance, this issue is the durable design ledger — the upstream google/adk-python submission will be a ~15K-character decision-oriented distillation in the #6357 shape, not a copy of this body.**
>
> *(Prior revision note, retained for context:)* **Revision 4.18** — resolving the seven P0 blockers and four P1 tightenings from the [Revision 4.17 review](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/BigQuery-Agent-Analytics-SDK/issues/406#issuecomment-5277166316). Changes: the mixed-batch rejection Event is **core-owned and skips the ordinary event callback** (resolving 4.17's runs-and-forbids contradiction); **user callbacks never execute on the registry thread** — model-path progress (and filters, header providers, trace, cancellation) marshal back to the owning operation/Runner loop, with transport I/O alone on the registry loop; Runner cleanup releases a **Runner-scoped registry lease token** (an argument-free shared `proxy.close()` cannot identify its caller); **legacy/stateful generation keys include the Session incarnation by default** (cross-Session sharing only by explicit profile opt-in with a declared server-handle contract); cold refresh gains a **host-private durable refresh-invocation record** (native tool, canonical argument bytes/locator, schema/catalog generation, classification revision — never public); batch admission becomes **two-phase** (an immutable batch-wide classification snapshot before any task, catching stale UI/non-UI metadata); and **export joins the governed-operation matrices** with an incarnation-bound permit, a final pre-release recheck, and **durable-before-release audit** (fail closed on audit failure). P1s: the `run()` wording is reconciled (pre-spawn rejection applies to same-session *reentry* only), production binding **rejects** fence-less backends (reduced durability is dev-only with its own acceptance matrix), the modern logical-binding claim is 7(f)-qualified everywhere including the success sentence, and id-order precedence is scoped to state deltas only. This remains a **draft for google/adk-python maintainers**; ratification items are in open question 7.
>
> *(Prior revision note, retained for context:)* **Revision 4.17** — resolving the six P0 blockers and three P1 tightenings from the [Revision 4.16 review](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/BigQuery-Agent-Analytics-SDK/issues/406#issuecomment-5276961136). Changes: the **registry owns a dedicated long-lived event loop for app-safe generations** (every listing/call/read/bootstrap/close marshals onto it, so a synchronous `run()`'s short-lived worker loop can no longer destroy the connection its View needs); app-safe generations are keyed by a **host-derived opaque security-domain key** (no legacy/stateful generation is ever shared across resolved principals); Session creation gains a **true write fence** (`create_if_fence_current` — a co-located fence row updated in the same transaction as the Session row, so a retired creator's late commit *fails*, not merely gets detected); mixed-batch rejection gains a **complete model-visible response contract** (one persisted Event with a terminal error FunctionResponse per original call id); cold **refresh is separated from rerun** (one-click refresh only for profile-classified replay-safe tools; otherwise an explicit "Run tool again" flow with confirmation and separate attribution); and cold non-View access moves to a **dedicated purpose-bound export resolver** (the View-bound resolver is unchanged). Stale 4.15 batch language is purged; registry-vs-Runner cleanup ownership is defined (non-owning proxies, reference release on `Runner.close()`); and the modern logical-binding reading of the same-connection rule is explicitly ratification-gated. This remains a **draft for google/adk-python maintainers**; ratification items are in open question 7. Earlier context from the Revision 4.16 note remains accurate below.
>
> *(Prior revision note, retained for context:)* **Revision 4.16** — resolving the six P0 blockers and four P1 tightenings from the [Revision 4.15 review](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/BigQuery-Agent-Analytics-SDK/issues/406#issuecomment-5276791815). Changes: connection affinity gains an **era-and-lifecycle matrix** (legacy generations are concrete client/session/process bindings; **modern stateless HTTP generations are host-side logical bindings — the sessionless 2026-07-28 core makes backend-instance affinity impossible by design**; cold replay after restart/eviction is defined as **explicit refresh/re-execution, not replay**, with sealed records remaining resolvable for authorized non-View consumption); the model's tool declaration is **pinned to the app-safe execution generation via a connection-bound tool handle** with pre-call re-listing; Session creation gains a **durable creation fence/receipt** persisted in the same transaction as the Session row (plus a distinct adoption receipt for migration); **mixed UI/non-UI parallel batches are rejected before fan-out** (replacing the backend-dependent non-UI narrowing — ledgering-all and batch-receipt designs are ratification 7(h)); interactive app-call results of UI-associated tools get an **Event-level sealed-result map** (`sealedResultRefs`, keyed by function-call id) alongside the per-widget reference; and readiness rebind becomes **monotonic** — the old proxy drives `REVOKING → CLOSED` and the registry atomically installs a newly constructed proxy under a new binding generation.
