items.body:
## Capability (cross-cutting foundation)
The single governed boundary to the LLM(s): every chat, streaming, and embedding call goes through one module so providers are swappable and answer quality is owned in one place. First pass makes the existing `backend/app/llm/` gateway real against **LiteLLM → OpenRouter** (ADR-0003 §7).

## Why this is Ready (needs-adr satisfied)
The gateway architecture is **decided** by [ADR-0003 §7](../blob/main/docs/architecture/0003-application-stack.md) (LiteLLM, OpenRouter first, swappable) and [ADR-0004](../blob/main/docs/architecture/0004-architecture-boundaries-and-adapters.md) (`backend/app/llm/` is the only model caller). No further ADR is needed for this scope; governance/routing (OUT, below) gets its own decision later. A boots-only skeleton already exists in `backend/app/llm/gateway.py` + `backend/app/domain/llm.py`.

## Stories satisfied
- [ ] Foundation for E2 (trusted answers) and E3 (assistant) — not a user story itself; traceability via the features it unblocks (#24, #29).

## Acceptance criteria  ← test plan
- [ ] AC-1: `LLMGateway.chat(messages, model=None)` returns a `Completion` domain object from a real OpenRouter call; model id comes from config when not passed.
- [ ] AC-2: `LLMGateway.stream(messages, …)` is an async generator yielding `CompletionChunk`s incrementally; breaking out of the consumer loop stops generation cleanly (cancellable).
- [ ] AC-3: `LLMGateway.embed(inputs, …)` returns one `Embedding` per input; vector dimension matches the configured embedding model (consumed by retrieval/ingestion #21).
- [ ] AC-4: model ids, timeout, and provider creds come from `core/config` only — switching `LLM_MODEL` (e.g. `openrouter/anthropic/claude-3.5-sonnet`) or provider needs **no code change**.
- [ ] AC-5: `Completion` carries token usage (prompt/completion/total) for later cost & observability.
- [ ] AC-6 (negative): blank `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` → typed `DependencyError` (→ 503 problem+json), never a hang or a raw LiteLLM traceback.
- [ ] AC-7 (negative): a provider error/timeout/unknown-model → mapped to a typed `AppError`; the original vendor exception never reaches the caller.
- [ ] AC-8 (boundary): callers receive only domain types — a test asserts no `litellm.*` object crosses the boundary and that `litellm` is imported **only** under `app/llm/`.

## Scope fences
- IN: chat · streaming · embeddings via LiteLLM→OpenRouter; config-driven model ids; request timeout; typed-error mapping; token-usage capture; unit tests (LiteLLM mocked) + one key-gated live smoke.
- OUT (later, own decision/ADR when needed): multi-model **routing/fallback** policy, **cost/budget limits & rate limiting**, **response caching**, **per-tenant model governance**, prompt management/versioning and **tool/function-calling** schema (those belong to CC-6 chat runtime #24). Per-tenant config keys off CC-2/CC-3 (OD-4).

## Dependencies
- blocked-by: none.
- blocks: #21 (ingestion needs `embed()`), #24 (chat runtime), #29 (grounded chat).

## Area / size / iteration
`area:model-gateway` · `size:M` · **iteration: M0** (pulled into M0 — M0 ingestion #21 depends on `embed()`).

## Implementation notes (first pass — for a junior)
Work **only** in `backend/app/llm/` (ADR-0004 boundary). Flesh out the existing skeleton; don't add `litellm` imports anywhere else.
1. **Domain types** (`app/domain/llm.py`, already stubbed): confirm `ChatMessage`, `Completion` (add `usage`), `CompletionChunk`, `Embedding`.
2. **Gateway** (`app/llm/gateway.py`): keep `litellm` imported lazily inside methods. Use `await litellm.acompletion(model=model_id, messages=[…], stream=…, api_key=…, timeout=settings.llm_timeout_seconds)` and `await litellm.aembedding(model=…, input=[…], api_key=…)`. OpenRouter is selected by the `openrouter/<vendor>/<model>` model-id prefix — no extra base-url config needed.
3. **Errors**: wrap calls; map `litellm.exceptions.*` (auth, rate-limit, timeout, bad-request) → `app.core.errors.DependencyError`/`ValidationError`. Never log `api_key`.
4. **Config** (`app/core/config.py`): add `llm_timeout_seconds` (default e.g. 60); `llm_model`/`llm_embedding_model`/`openrouter_api_key` already exist.
5. **Tests** (`backend/tests/test_llm_gateway.py`): monkeypatch `litellm.acompletion`/`aembedding` to assert (a) mapping to domain types, (b) streaming yields chunks and stops on break, (c) error mapping, (d) the no-vendor-leak/boundary check. Add a `@pytest.mark.skipif(no key)` live smoke that does one tiny real call.
6. **Think it through**: streaming must not leak tasks on cancel; embeddings go in one batched call; surface token usage; default model is config, never a literal.

## Definition of Done (AGENTS.md §15 + backend/AGENTS.md)
- [ ] ACs verified; `ruff`/`mypy --strict`/`pytest` green; boundary test passes; live smoke passes (or skipped with reason if no key).
- [ ] `backend/AGENTS.md` LLM-gateway section still accurate; no secrets logged.
- [ ] `docker compose up` still healthy.

items.body:
# Epic: database integration layer — close the schema-path / drift-oracle gap class

> **Epic.** #2356 and #2358 turned out to be two instances of one structural condition: **the generator paths that produce production DDL are not the paths tests exercise, and nothing compares a live database with what the model layer assumes.** A 2026-08-17 assessment of core, tenancy, migrations, the DDL strategies, the runtime query path and the system tables found the same shape in ~25 places, several larger than the original two. This epic tracks all of them, plus #2356/#2357/#2358, with a parallel-agent gameplan and a two-release landing plan.
>
> Full report (ranked findings, `file:line` evidence, what checked out, method): https://claude.ai/code/artifact/b67f605d-19fe-45cb-bbc8-b840d39eb080 — a Markdown copy is the first comment on this issue so it survives in tracker history. The report is also input for agent tuning; the "what future agents should do differently" list lands in `core/AGENTS.md` via #2381 and in the `repo-happyvertical-smrt` Hindsight bank.

## Why nobody noticed

```
@smrt() class ─▶ scanner ─▶ manifest.json ─▶ generateSTISchemaFromManifest / generateCTISchemaFromManifest ─▶ registry.schema ─▶ db:migrate   ◀ PRODUCTION
                                                (no FK/xref indexes, STI unique dropped, foreignKeys [], triggers [])
ObjectRegistry fields ─▶ generateSchemaFromRegistry / generateSTISchemaFromRegistry ─▶ getTestDatabase() (195 test files)              ◀ TESTS
                                                (FK + STI partial FK indexes — the ones prod lacks)
AST ─▶ generateSchema ─▶ virtual smrt:schema (no consumers)                                                                            ◀ DEAD

Live-DB oracles: runtime = tableExists() only · doctor = no DB connection · db:status/db:diff = diff against the manifest above
⇒ an index the manifest never emitted is, by construction, "in sync".
```

Headline numbers (schemas regenerated from current source, 238 tables): **196/231 `@foreignKey` and 91/92 `@crossPackageRef` columns unindexed in production; 118 tenant-scoped tables whose slug is unique across tenants; 238/238 tables carry a redundant PK index; 0 DB foreign keys; 0 live-schema parity checks.**

## Scope / children

| # | Issue | Area | Sev | Size | Wave |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | #2359 manifest paths emit reference-column indexes; STI unique; drop `_id_idx` — generalizes PR #2384's `ensureTenantIdIndex()` pattern (leads-with suppression) to `foreignKey`/`crossPackageRef` | core/schema | critical | L | 0 → critical path (rebase on #2384) |
| 2 | #2360 tenant-aware natural keys — conflict target + unique index include tenant; STI/custom-PK/report alignment | core/tenancy | critical | L | 1 (rebase on #2359) |
| 3 | #2361 commerce/products/facts money fields are INTEGER; knowledge-check lint | packages | critical | M | 0 |
| 4 | #2362 `db:migrate` PG lock/statement timeouts + concurrent-index mode (config live) | migrations/cli | high | M | 0 — **gates deploy of the schema wave** |
| 5 | #2363 index the generated default list ordering `(tenant_id, created_at)` | core/schema | high | S | 1 (after #2359) |
| 6 | #2364 hot poll/lookup predicates: `_smrt_jobs`, token hashes, `users.email`, junction right, polymorphic owner | jobs/users/profiles/assets/core | high | M | 0 (composites after #2357) |
| 7 | #2365 tenancy read gaps: get-by-slug, hydration, vector search, collection memory | core/tenancy | high | M | 0 |
| 8 | #2366 `save()`/load error contract dead; deterministic errors retried; 25P02 masking | core | high | M | 0 |
| 9 | #2367 query bounds: LIMIT 1, max limit, deterministic ORDER BY, orderBy sensitive check, chunked listByIds | core/generators | high | M | 0 |
| 10 | #2368 live-schema parity check (`doctor --db`/`db:status`) incl. system tables; fix decorators check | cli/core | high | M | 0 |
| 11 | #2369 differ: nullability/default drift, orphan NOT NULL report, executable ADD COLUMN | migrations | high | L | 0 |
| 12 | #2370 SQLite table-rebuild for type changes | migrations | medium | M | any |
| 13 | #2371 referential integrity decision; `delete()` cascade; `onDelete` real or removed | core | high | M | 0 (needs owner decision) |
| 14 | #2372 STI table shape independent of registration order | core/registry | medium | S | 0 |
| 15 | #2373 NUMERIC/BIGINT decision; PG BLOB→BYTEA | core/schema | medium | M | later (decision) |
| 16 | #2374 63-byte identifier guard; STI partial index naming | core/schema | medium | S | 2 (after #2359/#2363) |
| 17 | #2375 growth: `_smrt_ai_usage` prune API, scheduled prunes, prune-predicate indexes | core | medium | M | 0 (index part in schema wave) |
| 18 | #2376 system-table fresh==upgraded test; jobs compat on fresh installs; change-feed allowlist; dead tables | core | medium | M | 0 |
| 19 | #2377 runtime PG pool timeouts | core/sql | medium | S | 0 |
| 20 | #2378 `db:rollback` honesty | cli | medium | S | 0 |
| 21 | #2379 arrow-thunk `@foreignKey(() => X)` → `related: ''` | social/core | low | XS | 0 |
| 22 | #2380 remove dead generation surfaces; fix overclaiming docs | core/schema | low | S | 2 (after generator issues) |
| 23 | #2381 core/AGENTS.md schema-path invariants + agent lessons; Hindsight retain | docs | high | S | 0 |
| — | #2356 tenancy `tenant_id` index | core/schema | high | S | **PR #2384 open** (all four paths, `ensureTenantIdIndex()`); merges ahead of the epic — #2359 rebases on it |
| — | #2357 declared multi-column indexes on `@smrt()` | core/schema | high | S–M | 0 — first in the generator rebase order; branch already ~built, unblocker diagnosed (`schema/utils.ts:116-122`, `testing/database.ts:348-352` rebuild the config) |
| — | #2358 `schema.ddl` omits indexes | core/schema | medium | M | 0 — recommend reframing: route every consumer through the engine strategy and retire the DDL-string dialect (see report C3); implementer decides |

## Gameplan — minimum wall-clock with parallel sub-agents

**Pre-step (throughput).** Land #2383 (lane shape: shorter merge-group runs), then reconcile the merge-queue ruleset to policy per the plan on #2262 (`max_entries_to_build` 1 → 5 on the hosted lane; preflight currently blocked on the default-branch lifecycle canary). With the queue at 1 entry, this epic is ~25 sequential merge-group transits; at 5 it is ~5–6. Trains (integration branches) were considered and rejected as the primary lever — squash merges collapse per-issue attribution and the lifecycle tooling assumes small PRs; a single Release-2 train remains the fallback if the reconcile cannot land in time.

**Shape.** One coordinator session; one implementation agent per issue in an isolated worktree (`isolation: 'worktree'`, base pinned to the `origin/main` sha at spawn — agent worktrees otherwise spawn from repo HEAD), each running the standard `implement` lifecycle (claim → implement → validation → `review-cycle` → `ship`, PR closes its issue, release recorded). No stacked PRs (they get no validation). ~8–10 agents concurrently is the practical ceiling; **the binding constraint is CI + merge-queue throughput (one merge-group build at a time), not agent count**, so start everything that is independent on day 0 and keep the queue fed.

**Wave 0 — start immediately, all in parallel (independent files):** #2357, #2359, #2361, #2362, #2364 (single-column parts), #2365, #2366, #2367, #2368, #2369, #2371 (after the FK decision below), #2372, #2375, #2376, #2377, #2378, #2379, #2381, #2358 (as reframed or as filed), #2370.

**Wave 1 — as soon as #2359 merges:** #2363, #2360 (B1's registry/tenancy/manifest-normalization/differ-test work can start on day 0; only its generator hunk waits and rebases). #2364 composites once #2357 merges.

**Wave 2 — after #2359 and #2363:** #2374, #2380 (both edit near the same generator regions; small).

**Critical path:** #2384 (already open) → #2357 → #2359 → #2363 → #2374/#2380, and #2359 → #2360. Everything else hangs off the queue.

**Shared-file map (the only real serialization; everything else merges independently):**

| File | Issues | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `core/src/schema/generator.ts` | #2384 (open), #2357, #2359, #2363, #2360, #2374, #2380 | rebase in that order; each is additive to `indexes[]` so conflicts are small |
| `core/src/migrations/differ.ts` | #2369 (heavy), #2362 (add-index `IF NOT EXISTS`, light), #2368 (read-only via `SchemaComparer`, keep in a new module) | #2369 owns it; others keep hunks minimal |
| `core/src/object.ts` | #2366 (save/load retry), #2365 (loadFromId/Slug), #2371 (delete) | disjoint regions; parallel, rebase |
| `core/src/collection.ts` | #2367 (get/list/orderBy), #2365 (search/memory) | disjoint regions; parallel |
| `cli/src/commands/utilities.ts` | #2362, #2368, #2378 | different commands; parallel |
| `core/src/registry/schema-builder.ts` | #2372 (+ #2360 light) | #2372 first |
| `packages/*` models | #2361 (commerce/products/facts), #2364 (jobs/users/profiles/assets), #2379 (social) | disjoint |
| `core/AGENTS.md` | #2381 first; others append one line each | land #2381 early |

**Validation rules for this epic:** every generator PR adds cases to the path-parity test introduced by #2359 and attaches a `db:migrate` dry-run diff against an anytown-shaped PG snapshot; #2359/#2360/#2361/#2362/#2369 run the PostgreSQL lane, not only SQLite; no manual `.changeset/*.md`; worktree lefthook TTY failures → verify gates manually and push `--no-verify` (CI is the gate).

**Owner decisions needed before the affected agents start:** (a) #2371 — DB foreign keys now vs app-side cascade (recommendation: app-side now, DB FKs as a follow-up with topological ordering); (b) #2373 — `NUMERIC(p,s)` support vs integer-cents rule; (c) #2358 — retire the DDL-string dialect vs make the string complete; (d) #2360 — semantics for `mode: 'optional'` NULL-tenant rows.

## Release plan — two consumer upgrade windows

Releases cut daily by cron from whatever merged; the two external consumers (anytown, ergot) upgrade deliberately. "As few as reasonably safe" therefore means **two upgrade windows**, and — if the merges are staged so each wave lands within one calendar day — two version cuts:

**Release 1 — tooling & runtime (no schema change).** #2362, #2366, #2367, #2368, #2369, #2377, #2378, #2379, #2381, #2376 (non-schema parts), #2375 (scheduling), #2358, #2357 (capability only), #2370. *Why first:* consumers get bounded-timeout / concurrent migrate, the parity check, and the fixed error contract **before** absorbing the schema wave; the differ that computes the schema wave's migration is the fixed one.

**Release 2 — schema & semantics (one migration window).** #2359, #2363, #2364, #2361, #2372, #2374, #2375 (indexes), #2376 (jobs indexes), #2360, #2365, #2371, #2373 if decided. Consumers run `db:migrate` in the new concurrent mode in a maintenance window (~200 index builds on anytown), then the parity check. Release note calls out #2360 (per-tenant natural keys — ingestion flows that relied on cross-tenant dedup now insert per tenant) and #2371 (delete cascade).

**Fallback (Release 3):** only if #2360's PG-snapshot rehearsal isn't green in time — it ships alone with its own note. Everything else stays in the two windows.

**Rollout note for #2384:** it will land in a daily release before #2362 exists; consumers should apply that migration (~164 `CREATE INDEX` on anytown, one transaction, no lock timeout today) in a quiet window, or hold `db:migrate` until #2362 ships. Bundling all schema changes into one window is judged safe because: the new indexes are additive; #2360's new unique index is a superset key (cannot fail on existing data) and the differ swaps it in place by name; #2361's INTEGER→REAL is a whitelisted PG upgrade; and Release 1's parity check gives a same-day verification path.

## Out of scope (this epic)

- Emitting DB-level foreign keys (follow-up once #2371 decides and migration ordering exists)
- Keyset/cursor pagination (noted in #2367; later)
- Row-level security or per-tenant schemas
- #1905 (query diagnostics / EXPLAIN tooling) — related, not folded in

items.body:
> **This PRD spans three issues.** Section numbers are the PRD's own, so a reference
> such as §8, S5 or B11 means the same in all three.
>
> | Issue | Sections |
> |---|---|
> | **Forward provisioned user attributes to model providers as outbound headers** (parent) | §1–§5 summary, problem, scope, requirements (B1–B20), design decisions · §10–§12 size, PR sequencing, open questions (Q1–Q5) · Appendix A.4–A.14 |
> | **Persist the SCIM Enterprise User extension** (Part A) ← this issue | §6 Part A design · Part A tests (§9) · Appendix A.1–A.3 |
> | **Configurable outbound headers for self-hosted (vLLM) model providers** (Part B) | §7 Part B design · §8 security requirements (S1–S9) · §9 test plan · Appendix B |

Part A of the PRD: retain the SCIM Enterprise User extension that Eneo currently accepts and
discards, and advertise it in SCIM discovery. Correct on conformance grounds on its own, and
the prerequisite for Part B.

## 6. Part A — Persist SCIM extensions

### Data model

One nullable JSONB column on `users`, keyed by schema URN. The column shape is general; **what
v1 writes into it is not.**

> **v1 persists the enterprise extension and nothing else.** Storing every URN an IdP sends is
> tempting — storage is cheap, and it appears to avoid a migration when a directory adds a
> field. It does not: the column is JSONB, so admitting a second URN later is one allow-list
> constant, no schema change. Open storage buys nothing that closed storage cannot buy later on
> demand, and it costs something real — every persisted URN is personal data arriving at an
> authenticated endpoint and retained indefinitely that nobody at the deployment reviewed,
> widening the retention and subject-access surface, and leaving `/Schemas` advertising one
> extension while the database holds several (the untruth §A.3 exists to avoid).
>
> **Unknown URNs are accepted and ignored**, which RFC 7644 permits, rather than `400`-rejected —
> that would break an IdP sending an unrelated extension alongside the enterprise one, and Eneo
> has no standing to refuse data it simply does not use. The response `schemas` list reflects
> what was stored, so a client comparing request to response sees the difference, and ignored
> keys are logged at DEBUG (`scim.user.extensions_ignored`, names only) so an operator can tell
> what their IdP is sending.
>
> **Exposure is narrower still.** Part B's fixed six-token registry (§7) is a second boundary,
> not a restatement: persisting an attribute and making it forwardable to a third party are
> different decisions, and the second needs a code change and a review.

```python
# database/tables/users_table.py
scim_extensions: Mapped[Optional[dict[str, Any]]] = mapped_column(JSONB)
```

```json
{
  "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User": {
    "employeeNumber": "...",
    "costCenter":     "...",
    "organization":   "...",
    "division":       "...",
    "department":     "...",
    "manager":        { "value": "...", "$ref": "..." }
  }
}
```

An empty extension is stored as SQL `NULL`, never `{}`, so there is one representation of "none".
The URN key is matched case-insensitively.

**`manager.displayName` is read-only** — RFC 7643 §4.3 marks it `"mutability": "readOnly"`, the
server's to derive from the referenced user, not the client's to assert. Storing it raw would
mean echoing back a client-supplied value for an attribute Eneo never resolved.

So **persist `value` and `$ref`; drop `displayName` on ingest and do not echo it.** RFC 7644
§3.5.2 directs a server to ignore client-supplied read-only attributes, so this is the conformant
behaviour as well as the simpler one. Deriving it by resolving `value` against
`users.external_id` is out of scope: the reference may point at a user Eneo has never been
provisioned, and a half-populated `displayName` is worse than an absent one.

`manager` is deliberately not in the Part B registry — a dynamic value must resolve to a single
string, and picking one sub-attribute would bake an arbitrary choice into the schema.

### Migration

One revision chained onto the current head: additive, nullable, no backfill, no index — nothing
queries it yet. Downgrade drops the column; data loss is limited to re-syncable IdP-sourced data,
and the migration says so, as `202605261000` does for its own destructive downgrade.

### Ingestion

Set `model_config = ConfigDict(extra="allow")` on `ScimUserRequest`, then keep **only** the
enterprise extension URN. Because of `extra="allow"`, the ignored-keys log line lists any
unmodelled top-level key, core attributes such as `name` among them, not only URNs. The request's
`schemas` array is not used to decide what is stored: an extension object in the body is stored
even if its URN is missing from `schemas`.

#### Validation

Persistence alone is not conformance. A store-whatever-arrives implementation accepts
`{"costCenter": {"nested": "object"}}` and hands Part B's resolver something that is not a
string, to be defended against at every read.

- **Attribute names are case-insensitive** (RFC 7643 §2.1) — `costcenter`, `costCenter` and
  `COSTCENTER` are one attribute. Normalise to canonical casing on write, so the registry looks
  up one spelling and the column never holds two keys for one attribute. The same attribute, or
  the URN, sent twice in different casing is `400 invalidValue`.
- **Unknown attributes within a known URN are dropped** when they arrive inside an object value,
  as unknown URNs are. Named as a `PATCH` path, or as a fully qualified key in a path-less value,
  they are `400 invalidPath` (*PUT and PATCH*, below). `manager.displayName` follows the same
  split.
- **Types are checked.** `employeeNumber`, `costCenter`, `organization`, `division`,
  `department` are singular strings — a non-string is `400 invalidValue`, not a coerced `str()`.
  `manager` is an object with `value` / `$ref`; unknown sub-keys are dropped, and `$ref` is not
  checked to be a URI. A **bare string** `manager` is accepted and stored as `value`: IdPs send
  the manager reference that way in `PATCH`, and rejecting it would fail the whole atomic request
  and stall the sync. Anything else is `400 invalidValue`.
- **`null` means remove** (RFC 7644), and so does `""`. `{"department": null}` deletes the key
  rather than storing a JSON null, so the resolver has one representation of absent, not two.

#### Limits

Round numbers well clear of real directory data while still bounding the surface.

| Bound | Value | On breach |
|---|---|---|
| Serialised extension payload, total | 16 KiB | `400 invalidValue`, nothing written |
| Single attribute value | 1024 characters | `400 invalidValue`, nothing written |
| Attributes per URN | 64 | `400 invalidValue`, nothing written |

The per-value limit also applies to `manager.value` and `$ref`. The 16 KiB and 64-attribute
bounds apply to whole-object values — `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` on the URN, a path-less
`{URN: {…}}` — and count raw keys, unknown ones included; a single-attribute `PATCH` is bounded
by the per-value limit, and the stored object by the six known attributes.

`extra="allow"` on an authenticated endpoint with no bound is a storage-amplification vector;
these close it. The whole request is rejected rather than truncated, so a client is never told
`201 Created` about data that was silently trimmed — which is the same defect as Gap A.

#### `PUT` and `PATCH`

`PUT` replaces the extension map wholesale, consistent with replace semantics; an absent
extension clears it. `POST`'s reconcile-by-email and reactivation paths do the same.

`PATCH` is where the current code silently no-ops (§A.1), and it needs all three operations,
not just the assignment case:

| Operation | Path form | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `add` / `replace` | `urn:…:User:costCenter` (fully qualified) | Set that attribute |
| `add` / `replace` | `urn:…:User:manager.value`, `…:manager.$ref` | Set that sub-attribute |
| `add` / `replace` | no `path`, value is `{"urn:…:User": {…}}` or fully qualified keys | Merge the named attributes. Entra sends this form. |
| `add` / `replace` | `urn:…:User` (whole extension) | Merge the named attributes; others unchanged (RFC 7644 §3.5.2.3, complex target). A `null` value changes nothing |
| `remove` | `urn:…:User:costCenter` | Delete that attribute |
| `remove` | `urn:…:User` | Delete the whole extension object |

**`PATCH` is atomic.** RFC 7644 §3.5.2 requires that a request whose operations cannot all be
applied leaves the resource unchanged. Validate every extension operation in the request before
applying any operation, and fail the whole request on the first invalid one. A partially applied
`PATCH` is worse than a rejected one: the IdP believes it converged and will not retry.

**An unmatched extension path becomes an error, not a no-op.** Once `/Schemas` advertises the
extension, `PATCH` to `urn:…:User:noSuchAttribute` must return `400 invalidPath` — continuing to
no-op would recreate Gap A inside the feature that fixes it. So do a filter (`[…]`) and any
sub-attribute path other than `manager`'s. A path-less `remove` is ignored, operation names are
case-insensitive, and unknown operation names and paths on other extension URNs are ignored.
Whether unknown *core* attributes should also stop no-opping is a separate question (§12 Q1).

### Discovery and read surface

Persisting without advertising would make discovery incorrect, so `/Schemas` gains the
enterprise extension schema document and the `User` entry in `/ResourceTypes` gains a
`schemaExtensions` array with `"required": false`. `manager.$ref` is advertised as
`type: reference` with `referenceTypes: ["User"]`.

`ScimUser` responses echo **what was stored**, with the URN added to the response `schemas` list
(RFC 7644, for round-trip correctness). Deliberately not an echo of what was *sent*: an ignored
URN, a dropped unknown attribute, and a dropped `manager.displayName` are all absent from the
response, which is the only signal a client gets that they were not retained. A user without the
extension gets a response byte-identical to today's.

`UserInDB` gains `scim_extensions` and `external_id`; neither exists today and Part B needs both.
Both are `exclude=True`, so no response built from `UserInDB` exposes them, and `repr=False`, so
no log line that formats a user contains them. Extension values are **not** added to any
existing tenant-facing user API — they are provisioning data, read by the resolver and by SCIM
itself, the one exception being the audited preview endpoint (§7).

Bulk operations go through the same service methods, so they get the same handling per
operation; `bulkId:` references inside extension values are resolved like any other.

> **Part A is correct on its own.** Eneo currently accepts a documented SCIM payload, returns
> `201 Created`, and discards part of it; that conformance argument needs no reference to
> outbound headers. Until Part B exists nothing reads `scim_extensions` — it is stored, echoed
> over SCIM, and otherwise inert.

---

## 9. Test plan — Part A

The three test layers are described with the rest of §9, in the Part B issue.


| Case | Expected |
|---|---|
| Create with the enterprise extension | Stored under its URN; response echoes it and lists the URN in `schemas`. |
| Create without it | Column stays `NULL`; no behaviour change; response byte-identical to today. |
| Create with the enterprise extension **plus an unrelated URN** | Only the enterprise one stored; the response `schemas` list reflects that; the ignored URN logged by name. |
| Non-URN extra key | Not persisted. |
| `costcenter` / `COSTCENTER` | Normalised to canonical casing; the column never holds two keys for one attribute. |
| The same attribute twice, in different casing | `400 invalidValue`. |
| `costCenter` sent as an object or number | `400 invalidValue`, nothing written, no coercion. |
| `manager` with `displayName` | `value` and `$ref` stored; `displayName` dropped and not echoed. |
| `manager` as a bare string | Stored as `manager.value`. |
| `manager` as a number or list | `400 invalidValue`. |
| Unknown attribute inside the enterprise URN | Dropped inside an object value; the rest of the request applied. As a `PATCH` path, `400 invalidPath`. |
| Each limit at the boundary, and one past it | `400 invalidValue`, **nothing written** — not truncated. |
| `PUT` | Extension map replaced wholesale; absent extension clears it. |
| `PATCH replace` on a fully-qualified path | Value updated. Path-less dict form → same result. |
| `PATCH add` on an absent attribute | Added. |
| `PATCH replace` on the whole URN | Named attributes merged; others unchanged. |
| `PATCH remove` on an attribute / on the whole URN | Attribute deleted / object deleted. |
| `PATCH` with `{"department": null}` or `""` | Key removed, **not** stored as JSON null. |
| `PATCH`, valid operation then invalid one | **`400`, and the valid operation is not applied.** The atomicity test — assert the stored row is byte-identical to before. |
| `PATCH` on an unknown *extension* attribute | `400 invalidPath`, no longer a silent no-op. |
| Bulk | Same handling per operation; `bulkId:` references in extension values resolved. |
| Discovery | `/Schemas` and `/ResourceTypes` advertise the extension; `manager.displayName` carries `"mutability": "readOnly"`. |
| Migration | Up/down under `migration_isolation`. |

---

## Appendix A — Codebase findings: SCIM

Verified by reading source at `develop` @ `3df21f84c`, with `litellm==1.101.0` pinned in
`backend/pyproject.toml`. Line numbers will drift; the named symbols are the durable
references. The one assumption reading source cannot settle — that LiteLLM puts `extra_headers`
on the wire — is covered by Appendix B.

A.4–A.14 are in the parent issue.

### A.1 — SCIM silently discards unknown schema extensions

SCIM lives at `backend/src/eneo/scim/`, a `FastAPI` sub-application (`scim_app`) authenticated
per tenant against `tenants.scim_token_hash`.

`ScimUserRequest` (`scim/schemas/user.py:39`) is a plain Pydantic v2 `BaseModel` with no
`model_config`, so the v2 default `extra="ignore"` drops every enterprise-extension key during
validation; it never reaches `ScimUserService`. The inbound `schemas` list is accepted but never
checked, so an IdP declaring the extension URN gets no signal it was ignored.

`PATCH` has the same gap by a different route: `_apply_user_attr`
(`scim/services/user_service.py:513`) dispatches on a fixed set — `active`, `username`,
`externalid`, `emails` — and an unmatched attribute falls through as a silent no-op. Bulk
operations reuse the same schemas and inherit both behaviours.

### A.2 — No JSONB/metadata column on the user model · MIGRATION REQUIRED

`database/tables/users_table.py` has no JSON column; it gained `external_id` (VARCHAR, indexed,
partial-unique per tenant) in `202605261000_add_scim_schema`. JSONB is thoroughly idiomatic here
— roughly twenty tables use it, including `model_providers.config`, `audit_logs.metadata`,
`mcp_servers.http_auth_config_schema` — so a single nullable JSONB column on `users` matches
convention.

Separately: `UserInDB` (`users/user.py:266`) **does not expose `external_id`** even though the
column exists, so the registry's `user.externalId` token needs a Pydantic field added alongside
the new JSONB one.

### A.3 — SCIM discovery exists and is currently accurate

`/ServiceProviderConfig`, `/Schemas` and `/ResourceTypes` all exist in
`scim/resources/discovery.py` as hand-written documents. `/Schemas` returns core User and Group
only; `ResourceTypes` entries carry no `schemaExtensions` array.

Discovery is therefore currently *truthful* — Eneo correctly advertises that it does not support
the extension. Persisting extension data without updating both documents would make it lie, so
**both must change together**.

items.title: Add default raw-ingest Source for tenants with unknown repo shape

labels.name: developer-experience
labels.description: This improves the ease and fun of developing apps with neo.

items.body:
## Context

Tenth friction signal from the first-real-world cloud-deployment exercise (siblings neomjs/neo#12014 through neomjs/neo#12028). Surfaced while planning R3 tenant ingestion (the polling path for an external mirror repo as a first tenant smoke). To ingest an arbitrary tenant repo today, the operator must author a `CustomSource` per [CustomSources.md](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/agentos/cloud-deployment/CustomSources.md). For a "drop-in, just-let-me-see-what-happens" smoke against any unknown-shape repo, that is meaningful friction.

## The Problem

Neo's [`ai/services/knowledge-base/source/`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/tree/dev/ai/services/knowledge-base/source) ships 10 typed Source classes:

```
AdrSource          DiscussionSource   PullRequestSource
ApiSource          LearningSource     ReleaseNotesSource
ConceptSource      TestSource         TicketSource
SourceRegistry
```

Each is Neo-shape-specific:
- `LearningSource` enumerates `learn/`
- `AdrSource` enumerates `learn/agentos/decisions/`
- `TicketSource` enumerates `resources/content/issues/`
- `ApiSource` enumerates JSDoc output
- etc.

For an arbitrary tenant repo (a client tenant's product repo, a partner's checkout, an internal tooling repo), **none of these enumerators fit**. The operator's options today:

1. **Author a CustomSource** per `CustomSources.md` — meaningful upfront effort; requires understanding `parsed-chunk-v1` + the Source authoring contract; needs deployment-side wiring through `aiConfig.customSources` or `kb-config.yaml`. Right answer when the tenant's repo shape is *known* and ingestion ergonomics matter. Wrong answer for "let me ingest this and see what happens."

2. **Set `sourcePaths` overrides** on Neo's existing classes — only works if the tenant repo's shape happens to align with Neo's expectations (it almost never does for non-Neo repos).

3. **Manual per-file `ingest_source_files` MCP calls** — the Day-0 Milestone 2/4 path. Works file-by-file; doesn't scale beyond a smoke.

The parser layer already has a raw-text fallback per [Overview.md](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/agentos/cloud-deployment/Overview.md): *"with no parser match, the raw-text fallback ingests the whole file as one chunk"*. But the Source layer has no equivalent — there's no Source class that just enumerates every file in a repo and lets the parser-layer fallback handle the content.

## The Architectural Reality

This is a **Source-class gap, not a Parser-class gap**. Distinct from neomjs/neo-agent-brain#149 (which is about deepening parser coverage across more file formats — the per-format depth of parsing). This ticket is about the enumeration layer one level up.

Affected:
- `ai/services/knowledge-base/source/` — needs a new class (e.g., `RawRepoSource`).
- `SourceRegistry` — needs to register it as a built-in.
- `aiConfig` default-source defaults — needs a decision: does the new Source become a default for `useDefaultSources: true`, OR is it specifically the fallback for tenant configs that don't register any Source?
- `kb-config.yaml` schema — may need a `defaultRawIngest: true` flag (or implicit-when-no-customSources behavior).

## The Fix — proposed shape

Add `RawRepoSource` (working name) under `ai/services/knowledge-base/source/`:

- **Enumeration**: recursively walks the configured repo root, emits each file as a chunk-source.
- **Filter**: respects a configurable allow/deny list (e.g., default-deny on `.git`, `node_modules`, `dist`, binary file extensions). Sensible defaults so a first-time operator gets reasonable behavior.
- **Parser dispatch**: hands each file to the existing parser registry. With no registered parser match, falls through to the raw-text parser (the existing parser-layer fallback). One chunk per file.
- **Chunk metadata**: stamps `parsedChunks[].sourcePath` with repo-relative path; `kind` defaults to `'raw'` or matches the file extension when known (e.g., `.md` → `'doc-section'`); `name` is the basename.

**Defaulting behavior** — implementer's call between two shapes:

| Option A | `RawRepoSource` becomes a built-in default that fires when a tenant has `useDefaultSources: false` AND no `customSources` registered. Implicit fallback. |
| Option B | `RawRepoSource` exists but tenants must explicitly opt in via `customSources: [{SourceClass: 'RawRepoSource'}]` or a new `rawRepoSource: true` flag. Explicit. |

Option A is closer to the user's "drop in as-is parser, and that should be the default" framing — but raises a small risk that operators forget they're using it and don't author a better CustomSource later. Option B requires more explicit operator opt-in, more boilerplate-y, but never surprises.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ai/services/knowledge-base/source/RawRepoSource.mjs` (new) | This ticket; existing Source authoring contract per CustomSources.md | Walks the repo tree, emits each file as a chunk-source, defers to parser-registry for content parsing (raw-text fallback always available) | None — currently no fallback exists at the Source layer | `CustomSources.md` extension naming this as a built-in, distinct from custom authoring | Existing 10 Source classes confirmed via `ls ai/services/knowledge-base/source/`; none generic |
| `SourceRegistry` default-source set | `aiConfig.useDefaultSources` | Register `RawRepoSource` as part of the default registry OR as the no-custom-sources fallback | Implementer's call between Option A (implicit default) and Option B (explicit opt-in) | Configuration.md table of default Source classes | Currently 10 Sources, all Neo-shape-specific |
| `kb-config.yaml` schema | `KnowledgeBaseTenantConfig` shape per neomjs/neo#11637 | If Option B chosen, add a new field (`rawRepoSource: true` or via `customSources` entry); if Option A, no schema change | None | `Configuration.md` per-tenant config docs | Existing per-tenant fields documented in Configuration.md |

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0014` — completes the tenant-ingestion ergonomic story under existing cloud-topology authority. No ADR successor risk.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New Source class exists under `ai/services/knowledge-base/source/` that enumerates an arbitrary repo tree and emits chunk-sources per file.
- [ ] Defaulting behavior chosen + documented (Option A or B per Fix section).
- [ ] At least one configurable file-filter (allow/deny list or extension filter) with sensible defaults that skip `.git`, `node_modules`, common binary formats.
- [ ] `kb-config.yaml` can configure a tenant to use it (whether implicitly or explicitly per chosen Option).
- [ ] Smoke test: configure a tenant pointing at any small public repo (or `neomjs/create-app` test fixture), run ingestion, verify chunks present in KB with `sourcePath` reflecting the repo tree.
- [ ] `CustomSources.md` updated with a "when to use built-in raw-ingest vs author a custom Source" decision section.

## Out of Scope

- Per-format parser coverage — that's neomjs/neo-agent-brain#149. This ticket adds an ENUMERATOR; parser-layer raw-text fallback already handles unknown formats.
- Sophisticated file filtering (gitignore-respect, .dockerignore-respect, etc.) — basic deny-list is enough for v1; revisit when operators report friction.
- Tenant-specific path overrides via `sourcePaths` — the existing override surface stays for Neo-shape-aligned tenants; raw-ingest is for arbitrary-shape tenants.
- Server-side clone / fetch concerns — deferred to neomjs/neo#11731.

## Avoided Traps

- Naming as `GenericSource` — rejected; "generic" doesn't communicate the as-is/walk-the-tree intent. `RawRepoSource` or `WalkRepoSource` more accurately describes the enumerator behavior.
- Conflating Source-enumeration with Parser-content-parsing — rejected; they're separate layers (per Overview.md "Source vs Parser" split). The fix is at the Source layer.
- Coupling to the Default-Source registry too tightly (Option A only) — rejected for blanket adoption; defaults need careful thought + may belong in a separate `defaultRawIngest` config field.

## Related

- ADR 0014 — cloud-deployment topology authority.
- neomjs/neo#11658 (Phase 0/1B registry) — established the SourceRegistry; this ticket adds a new registered class.
- neomjs/neo-agent-brain#149 — sibling parser-coverage-deepening (distinct concern; parser depth, not source enumeration).
- neomjs/neo#11726 — tenant-repo ingestion operational model (consumer of this).
- neomjs/neo#11791 — operator docs + health/telemetry for tenant-repo ingestion (downstream documentation consumer).
- neomjs/neo#12014, neomjs/neo#12015, neomjs/neo#12016, neomjs/neo#12017, neomjs/neo#12019, neomjs/neo#12022, neomjs/neo#12025, neomjs/neo#12026, neomjs/neo#12028 — sibling friction tickets from the first-real-world cloud-deployment exercise.

## Handoff Retrieval Hints

- Grep: `ls ai/services/knowledge-base/source/` — pre-fix shows 10 typed Sources; post-fix adds one generic.
- Semantic: "raw-ingest Source default tenant arbitrary repo shape", "drop-in Source no custom authoring".
- File anchor: `ai/services/knowledge-base/source/` directory.

items.title: portal: enforce application-level per-tenant rate, concurrency and workload budgets for protected APIs
items.body:
## Finding

**Severity:** MEDIUM
**Modules:** Identity, bot lifecycle, terminal, administration, model/AI, Strategy Lab and high-cost read APIs
**Completeness status:** MISSING / ABUSE-RESISTANCE GAP
**Detected on:** `626087ca45d67eb908d6c1f1f419f13cbd49f596`

The security architecture requires risk-based WAF/rate-limit families and per-tenant limits. The repository currently validates only that a staging policy document names required Cloudflare families. It does not define or enforce thresholds, keying, burst/sustained behavior or application-level per-tenant/concurrency budgets. No common `429`/quota implementation was found in the Portal application.

## Expected behavior

Every protected API family must have an explicit workload budget combining, as appropriate:

- per-tenant and per-actor/service sustained rate;
- bounded burst;
- in-flight concurrency;
- expensive-operation/job quotas;
- request/response/body/cardinality limits;
- stable retry metadata and fail-closed overload behavior;
- distributed coordination for multiple replicas;
- edge controls as defense in depth, not the sole tenant-aware authority.

Budgets must be route/action-specific. Reads, idempotent status polling and high-impact mutations cannot share one naive global bucket.

## Actual behavior

- `SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md` lists high-priority route families and states webhook ingestion requires per-tenant rate limits.
- `deploy/cloudflare/schema.py` defines enum names such as authentication, exchange credentials, bot lifecycle, terminal intent, model promotion and admin.
- `deploy/cloudflare/policy.py` verifies only that all enum values appear in a policy document; it contains no threshold, period, key, burst, action or deployed-rule identifier.
- no application token bucket, quota store, semaphore, concurrency middleware, `Retry-After` producer or canonical `429` handling was found.
- expensive paths include:
  - dashboard/multi-source aggregation;
  - unbounded or full-scan collections identified in #1107;
  - Strategy Lab experiment creation and large result reads;
  - AI/model/telemetry operations;
  - terminal intent and bot lifecycle mutations;
  - exchange verification/administration;
  - audit/log/search reads;
  - public login-flow creation (#1128) and signed signal ingress (#1095).
- outbound adapters understand provider `429`, but the Portal does not protect its own resources with equivalent inbound budgets.
- current SQLite deployment increases contention impact because protected reads also touch session state and writes serialize (#1122).

## Evidence

- Audit PR: #1082
- Audited product base: `626087ca45d67eb908d6c1f1f419f13cbd49f596`
- Requirements: `docs/ai_platform/portal/SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md`, section **WAF and rate-limiting policy families**
- Declarative policy only: `ai_platform/portal/deploy/cloudflare/schema.py`; `policy.py`; `tests/ai_platform/portal/deploy/cloudflare/test_policy.py`
- No application limiter/quota implementation found in Portal code/tests
- Request/collection/transport limits: #1115, #1107 and #1110
- Public login and signal-specific gaps: #1128 and #1095
- Database/session contention: #1122
- API-mode/protected-target acceptance: #1098 and #1089

## Impact

One authenticated user, compromised session, noisy automation or accidental retry loop can monopolize database connections, CPU, memory or provider calls for an entire tenant or deployment. Edge IP-based rules cannot reliably express authenticated tenant/actor/service quotas, and a single global application bucket could let one tenant deny service to others. High-impact mutations also need different treatment from safe reads and polling.

## Required work

- Create a canonical route/action workload inventory with cost class, auth scope, rate, burst, concurrency, queue and retry policy.
- Implement a shared application limiter keyed by tenant plus actor/service/endpoint identity as appropriate, with an emergency global protection layer.
- Use durable/distributed coordination for multi-instance limits where correctness matters; document local-only limits used solely as process protection.
- Add per-operation concurrency limits and asynchronous job admission for expensive Strategy Lab/model/administrative work.
- Integrate request body, pagination, response-size and polling budgets from #1115/#1107/#1110/#1119.
- Return a versioned safe `429`/overload envelope with bounded `Retry-After`, request/correlation ID and no resource/tenant enumeration.
- Ensure idempotent mutation status recovery remains possible without allowing unlimited polling or automatic side-effect replay.
- Configure and verify corresponding Cloudflare/WAF rules with explicit rule IDs/thresholds/evidence, while keeping application tenant-aware controls authoritative.
- Emit low-cardinality metrics for accepted/rejected/in-flight/queued work and alert on sustained saturation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every protected/public API family has a documented rate/concurrency/workload budget or explicit not-applicable justification.
- [ ] Per-tenant and per-actor/service limits prevent one tenant from exhausting all normal capacity while a bounded emergency global limit remains.
- [ ] Expensive experiment/model/admin operations have separate admission/concurrency/queue limits from lightweight reads.
- [ ] Terminal, lifecycle, credential and admin mutations fail before side effects when over limit and are never automatically replayed unsafely.
- [ ] Safe status/read polling uses bounded conditional/backoff behavior and cannot create a thundering herd.
- [ ] Limits work across multiple application instances and survive restart where required.
- [ ] `429`/overload responses carry stable safe codes and bounded retry metadata without revealing bucket state for another tenant/user.
- [ ] Edge WAF/rate-limit evidence includes exact deployed rules/thresholds and direct-origin/application tests prove defense in depth.
- [ ] Tests cover burst, sustained, concurrency, one-noisy-tenant isolation, multi-instance race, recovery and limit-store outage.
- [ ] Limit-store failure follows a documented fail-open/fail-closed decision per route family; high-impact mutations fail closed.
- [ ] Metrics use bounded labels and do not expose attacker-controlled identifiers, secrets or private endpoints.
- [ ] Exact-image, API-mode and protected-target load/security tests pass on the implementation head.

## Safety boundary

Rate limiting must never replace authentication, authorization, risk or idempotency checks; leak tenant/user existence; trust unverified proxy headers; create one globally attacker-exhaustible bucket; or turn overload acknowledgement into execution proof/live-capital authority.

## Audit boundary

This is an implementation task created from the continuing audit in PR #1082. The audit PR must not implement the product change.
